# International regimes
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/international
description: How rules for tokenized securities differ outside the US, region by region.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-11-20

*In plain English: How rules for tokenized securities differ outside the US, region by region.*

**EU [[concepts/glossary#dlt|DLT]] Pilot Regime**: ESMA's 2025 review found low uptake, with only [[concepts/glossary#csd|CSD]] Prague, 21X and 360X authorised; barriers include thresholds, interoperability, central-bank money and legal uncertainty. ESMA recommends making the regime permanent and wider ([ESMA report](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-06/ESMA75-117376770-460_Report_on_the_functioning_and_review_of_the_DLTR_-_Art.14.pdf); [ESMA press](https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/esma-suggests-amendments-dlt-pilot-regime-make-it-permanent)).
**UK tokenised collateral at CCPs**: on 29 Oct 2026 the Bank of England consulted on draft supervisory expectations for clearing houses (CCPs) that want to accept tokenised versions of collateral they can already take. It says current rules are no barrier and creates no new regime; the token must still be valued, moved and sold when needed, including in stress. Responses close 12 Feb 2027 ([Bank of England CP](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/paper/2026/cp/supervisory-expectations-for-ccps-seeking-to-accept-tokenised-collateral)).
**UK enabling amendment (Woolard letter, 18 Nov 2026)**: Chris Woolard, the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion, wrote to the Economic Secretary to the Treasury welcoming an amendment the government had laid to the Financial Services and Markets Bill, "which will enable legislation to adapt to technological change." He highlighted "the need for greater clarity for settlement finality" and "the treatment of registers in the Companies Act, which could prevent the issuance of digitally native equities." His second report is due in July 2027. The letter says the government has laid the amendment; it does not say the amendment has been enacted ([letter](https://www.theglobalcity.uk/PositiveWebsite/media/research-downloads/20261118_CW-Letter.pdf)).
**EU central bank money settlement (Pontes)**: on 26 Oct 2026 the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) settled a €1bn digital benchmark bond through Pontes, the Eurosystem platform that settles DLT trades in central bank money (live since 21 Sep 2026). Clearstream ran the bond on its D7 DLT platform with the cash leg paid in TARGET (T2); the Bundesbank was issuing and paying agent. The bond can move to traditional settlement via T2S and is expected to be eligible as Eurosystem and Eurex collateral ([Deutsche Börse release](https://www.deutsche-boerse.com/dbg-en/media/news-stories/press-releases/ESM-is-first-European-supranational-issuer-to-settle-DLT-based-bond-issuance-on-Eurosystem-s-Pontes-platform-with-Bundesbank-and-Clearstream-5660764)).
**South Korea**: revised securities laws recognise security tokens as securities from 4 Feb 2027. The FSC's Sep 2026 roadmap starts with institutional money market funds and bonds, unlisted stocks via trusts and public fractional securities, then all public securities, then stablecoin-linked on-chain payments ([FSC roadmap](https://fsc.go.kr/eng/pr010101/87653)). Draft rules (comments to 11 Nov 2026) require ledgers shared by two or more account managers plus the central depository KSD, let issuers run customer accounts with KRW4bn of equity, and cap retail buying at KRW100m net a year per OTC exchange ([FSC draft rules](https://fsc.go.kr/eng/pr010101/87834)).
**Australia**: the Reserve Bank of Australia consulted (3 Sep to 30 Oct 2026) on how its settlement system RITS could support tokenised markets: linking token platforms to RITS for [[concepts/glossary#dvp|DvP]], at-par exchange of tokenised money, reserve access for [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]] issuers, and tokenised reserves. It sets out asset-lock, reserves-lock and combined-lock models without choosing one. This is a payments paper, not a securities rule ([RBA consultation paper](https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/tokenised-money/the-role-of-rits-in-supporting-settlement-in-a-tokenised-ecosystem/pdf/the-role-of-rits-in-supporting-settlement-in-a-tokenised-ecosystem.pdf)).
**Singapore / US tokenized-deposit rails (cash leg):** on 16 Nov 2026 DBS and Kinexys by J.P. Morgan launched a commercially ready interoperability link for instant USD transfers between blockchain-based accounts in Singapore and the United States, including on weekends. This is tokenized commercial-bank money, not a tokenized security; see [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]] ([DBS release](https://www.dbs.com/newsroom/DBS_and_Kinexys_by_JP_Morgan_launch_industry_first_247_interoperability_solution_for_cross_border_tokenised_deposit_transfers)).
**US ZelleUSD stablecoin (cash leg):** on 16 Nov 2026 Zelle demonstrated a $1.25 million confidential ZelleUSD transfer on Solana devnet at Breakpoint, between demo banks labeled Bank Alpha and Bank Beta. This is a [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]] cash-leg example, not a tokenized deposit or a tokenized security; see [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]. Zelle's 11 June 2026 release said India would be the first country where U.S. consumers can use Zelle to send money overseas, with initial availability expected before the end of 2026, but that release does not say the corridor uses ZelleUSD, and no launch date has been given ([Zelle release](https://www.zelle.com/press-releases/zelle-heads-to-india-unveils-zelleusdsm-stablecoin-other-markets), [@solana](https://x.com/solana/status/2122284580405236216)).
**Global (IOSCO, Nov 2026)**: IOSCO's 2026 monitoring report says regulators are converging on legal certainty of token ownership, alignment of onchain and offchain records, custody, disclosure of investor rights, resilience, and governance of smart contracts, bridges and oracles. On stock tokens it says authorities stress distinguishing tokenized shares that confer shareholder rights from products that only give price exposure, which may fall under derivatives, structured-product or other frameworks ([IOSCO 2026](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD832.pdf)).
**Singapore / Germany (Project Simbolon, cash leg)**: on 16 Nov 2026 MAS and the Deutsche Bundesbank reported a proof of concept for atomic euro/Singapore-dollar payment-versus-payment across two separate central-bank test ledgers, linked by zero-knowledge proofs rather than a shared ledger or trusted intermediary ([MAS release](https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2026/mas-and-deutsche-bundesbank-advance-cross-border-digital-asset-settlement-connectivity); [insights note](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/development/fintech/project-simbolon/project-simbolon-insights-note.pdf)). See [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]].
**Hong Kong (Project Ensemble and Swift)**: on 16 Nov 2026 the HKMA said it is continuing work with Swift, Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered Hong Kong and HSBC to explore interoperability between the Swift ledger and Project Ensemble's settlement layer for multi-currency tokenised-deposit cross-border payments. This is exploration of the cash leg, not a live service ([HKMA](https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/11/20261116-4/)).
**Hong Kong (HSBC RedCoin tokenised fund access):** on 19 Nov 2026 HSBC said eligible customers can use HSBC RedCoin (RCHKD), its licensed Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, in the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App to buy Class SD, a new tokenised unit class of the HSBC Global Money Funds – Hong Kong Dollar, from a minimum of HKD 100 (funded with RCHKD 100). HSBC's Securities Services tokenises the class, and its Digital Assets Custody safekeeps both the stablecoin and Class SD. This is a tokenised money market fund, not a tokenized stock ([HSBC](https://www.about.hsbc.com.hk/news-and-media/hsbc-redcoin-expands-into-wealth-with-tokenised-fund-access)).
**Offshore issuer domiciles** in this wiki: Jersey (xStocks, Robinhood), BVI (Ondo), ADGM (bStocks, Coinbase). See [[topics/regulation|regulation]].
**EU DLT Pilot Regime venues (Oct to Nov 2026)**: 21X AG, which describes itself as the first venue licensed under the Pilot Regime to run both trading and settlement, ran a month-long pilot of its fully onchain order book with LayerZero on a private Zero instance; it reports 10,000 order matches per second (company-reported, [21X](https://21x.eu/21x-ag-and-layerzero-deliver-institutional-grade-onchain-trading-pilot-on-private-permissioned-deployment-of-zero/)); see [[platforms-venues/21x|21X]]. On 20 Oct 2026 Boerse Stuttgart Group obtained a DLT trading and settlement system licence from BaFin for Seturion, which lets connected venues offer tokenized assets without their own DLT licence ([Boerse Stuttgart](https://group.boerse-stuttgart.com/en/seturion-blog/boerse-stuttgart-group-obtains-dlt-tss-license-and-lays-regulatory-basis-for-seturion/)); see [[platforms-venues/seturion|Seturion]].
**Dubai (DFSA)**: on 5 Nov 2026 the DFSA published a white paper, *Scaling Tokenisation: The Road Ahead*, on custody, digital settlement, interoperability and cross-border coordination; it says it is not a consultation, policy statement or guidance ([DFSA](https://www.dfsa.ae/news/dfsa-launches-scaling-tokenisation-road-ahead)).
**EU funds (Amundi)**: on 5 Nov 2026 Amundi announced a tokenised share class of a flagship European equity index fund on public Ethereum, built with CACEIS's tokenisation technology and kept within the fund's existing operating model ([Amundi](https://about.amundi.com/article/amundi-extends-tokenisation-index-investing)).
**EU Tokenisation Standards Group**: on 9 Nov 2026 the ECB, the European Commission and ESMA called for nominations to a new industry-chaired European Tokenisation Standards Group, with the three authorities as observers, to develop common standards for an interconnected tokenised financial ecosystem and a framework to monitor compliance. Applications are due 27 Nov 2026 ([ESMA](https://www.esma.europa.eu/press-news/esma-news/eu-seeks-nominations-stakeholder-group-tokenisation-standards-finance)).
**Ireland (Central Bank of Ireland, DP12 feedback):** in November 2026 the Central Bank of Ireland published a Feedback Statement to Discussion Paper 12 on DLT and tokenisation, with five priority areas led by central bank money settlement and the collateral framework, placed alongside EU reforms (including proposed DLT Pilot Regime changes and replacing the Settlement Finality Directive with a regulation) and the Eurosystem's Pontes and Appia work ([Central Bank of Ireland](https://www.centralbank.ie/docs/default-source/publications/discussion-papers/discussion-paper-12/feedback-statement-discussion-paper12.pdf?sfvrsn=b6b0741a_16)).
**Bermuda**: on 6 Nov 2026 the Bermuda Monetary Authority published a stakeholder letter on its April 2026 asset-tokenisation consultation. It intends to amend existing laws rather than create a separate tokenisation regime, with a single harmonised definition of "tokenised investment" in the Investment Business Act 2003, cross-referenced by the funds, fund administration, DABA and DAIA acts; both "digital twin" and "native token" models recognised, with model-specific expectations; and three functional roles retained (Primary Tokeniser, Secondary Offeror, Custodian). It will not prescribe a chain or token standard. Guidance is to cover cross-chain and bridging risk. The Authority noted feedback that autonomous protocols and non-custodial software should not be treated as Secondary Offerors solely because they facilitate transactions. Legislation, guidance and a transition roadmap are still to come ([BMA](https://www.bma.bm/viewPDF/documents/2026-11-06-14-04-05-Stakeholder-Letter---Feedback-on-the-Consultation-Paper-on-Asset-Tokenisation.pdf)).
**Cambodia**: on 13 Nov 2026 SBI Holdings said it had signed an MOU with the National Bank of Cambodia for a proof of concept on tokenizing Cambodian government bonds on the Canton Network. Under the MOU, the central bank would register and manage bondholder records as tokens transfer; SBI Bank (Cambodia) and SBI Digital Practice would build and run the test environment. The stated aim is small-unit retail holdings through local banks. This is an MOU for a PoC, not a live service; service details and timing are still to be decided ([SBI Holdings](https://www.sbigroup.co.jp/news/pdf/2026/1113_a.pdf)).
**Japan**: the Financial Services Agency has convened a FY2026 study group on digital and decentralised finance, under an "on-chain finance" forum that targets an interim summary and public-private roadmap in early 2027. Topics include stablecoins and tokenised deposits, security tokens (including tokenised stocks and MMFs), DEX/DeFi and wallet providers, the book-entry transfer system, and faster securities settlement. The 20 Oct 2026 secretariat deck says on-chain trading of book-entry securities (JGBs, corporate bonds, investment trusts, stocks and the like) has not been realised in Japan, while domestic tokenisation has begun to broaden from a focus on real-estate securitisation products. It cites a Nomura, Daiwa and three-megabank on-chain DvP pilot, and a "Tokenised Stocks / Tokenised Law WG" set up in November 2025 through the Digital Asset Co-Creation Consortium, whose secretariat is Progmat, Inc. Official agendas record hearings from Nomura Holdings and Securitize Japan (20 Oct 2026) and from JPYC, SBI VC Trade and the Japanese Bankers Association (2 Nov 2026). This is an agenda, not rules ([FSA deck](https://www.fsa.go.jp/singi/digital_2026/shiryo/261020/jimukyoku.pdf); [study group page](https://www.fsa.go.jp/singi/digital_2026/index.html)).
Not yet collected: MiCA/[[concepts/glossary#mifid-ii|MiFID II]] detail, UK [[concepts/glossary#digital-securities-sandbox|Digital Securities Sandbox]], Swiss DLT Act, Singapore and Hong Kong securities rules (the Singapore and Hong Kong items above are cash-leg projects and a tokenised fund, not those rule texts).

For one table of rules by country, see [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].

# Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition
description: Industry working group formed by Bullish and Equiniti in Sep 2026 to set standards for issuer-sponsored tokenized securities.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-11-17

*In plain English: A group of exchanges, brokers and market firms working on rules and plumbing so companies can put their own shares onchain, with holders keeping the same rights as normal shareholders.*

Bullish and Equiniti formed the Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition on 24 Sep 2026, a week after the SEC's [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)). It backs the [[concepts/glossary#issuer-sponsored-token|issuer-sponsored token]] model, where the token is tied to the company's official shareholder register kept by its [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

## Members
- **Founding (24 Sep 2026):** Bullish and Equiniti, with Alpaca, Apex Fintech Solutions and DriveWealth ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).
- **Joined 26 Oct 2026:** Qube Research & Technologies (QRT), [[infrastructure/vertalo|Vertalo]] and [[infrastructure/zerohash|zerohash]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join)).
- **Joined 17 Nov 2026:** DRW (via Cumberland, its digital asset business), Flow Traders, SoFi and [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]] ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-token-coalition-surges-to-12-firms-as-drw-flow-traders-sofi-and-superstate-join)).

With these additions the coalition has 12 firms. The 17 Nov 2026 release calls the group the "Issuer Token Coalition"; earlier releases used "Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition", and this page keeps that name (Bullish release of 17 Nov 2026, linked in the member list above; [Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-token-coalition-surges-to-12-firms-as-drw-flow-traders-sofi-and-superstate-join)).

Membership is open, non-exclusive and non-binding: joining does not commit a firm to issue, list, provide liquidity or support any product ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

Founding members Alpaca, Apex (as Apex Clearing Corporation) and DriveWealth are also among the 20 DTC participants signed for the DTCC Tokenization Service at its 28 Oct 2026 launch ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]]; [DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)).

## Focus areas
1. Keep issuer and shareholder rights, including [[concepts/glossary#corporate-action|corporate-action]] entitlements.
2. Interoperability across traditional clearing and settlement, blockchains, [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]]-token models and emerging [[concepts/glossary#entitlement-token|entitlement-token]] frameworks. Example: Securitize's convertible entitlement token, which converts to a registered share once the issuer sponsors tokenization ([[issuers/securitize|Securitize]]).
3. Infrastructure for issuance, transfer, settlement, custody and trading.
4. An open ecosystem of issuers, brokers, exchanges, transfer agents, custodians and market makers.

([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities))

## Getting shares onto the register
Issuer-sponsored tokens need shares moved out of [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]]'s nominee [[concepts/glossary#cede--co|Cede & Co.]] and into the holder's own name, via the [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]]. DTC has proposed cutting DRS processing "from days to minutes" ([SEC notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change)). The SEC notice gave an expected implementation date of 13 Nov 2026, and no later than January 2027. On 6 Nov 2026, DTC postponed that November 2026 implementation; subject to regulatory approval, it expects to implement no later than 30 Jun 2027, and will announce the specific date in a later Important Notice ([DTC notice B#25240-26](https://files.dtcc.com/download/assets/25240-26/306b2894da2f11f192c2a2d2c72ada28)). Securitize's comment letter asks DTC to link DRS to its own tokenization service and publish processing times ([[issuers/securitize|Securitize]]; [Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf)).

## What's next
Bullish and Equiniti hosted an issuer briefing in the NYSE Boardroom on 27 Oct 2026 ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join)). The agenda compared issuer-sponsored, infrastructure-sponsored and third-party token models and covered shareholder rights, the official ownership record, corporate actions and a US regulatory update. Equiniti's stated position is that the transfer agent stays the legal record of ownership and the blockchain is a representation layer, not the system of record ([Equiniti](https://equiniti.com/us/public/transfer-agent-services/equiniti-x-tokenization/); [Equiniti event overview](https://equiniti.com/media/n0woocck/equiniti_x_bullish_nyse_event_overview.pdf)). More members and initiatives were promised "in the coming weeks" ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

Founding member Equiniti also joined NYSE's network of transfer agents for issuer-sponsored tokens on 2 Nov 2026, alongside Broadridge, Computershare, Superstate (which joined the coalition on 17 Nov 2026), Securitize and tZERO ([[platforms-venues/nyse-ice-tokenized-platform#transfer-agent-partners|NYSE / ICE]]; [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/nyse-expands-tokenization-push-with-firms-serving-nearly-99-of-sp-500/)).

The 17 Nov 2026 release says the coalition's next phase will define standards through collaboration work streams, including liquidity mechanics, standards and tech architecture, and building out a commercially viable ecosystem to support issuer tokens. Flow Traders' Ruben Brons said the firm is joining to bring "a liquidity provider's view on what it takes for them to be reliably liquid, including when traditional markets are closed" (Bullish release of 17 Nov 2026, linked in the member list above; [Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-token-coalition-surges-to-12-firms-as-drw-flow-traders-sofi-and-superstate-join)).

Why Bullish is backing this: see [[platforms-venues/bullish#why-it-matters|Bullish: Why it matters]].

Related: [[platforms-venues/bullish|Bullish]] · [[topics/legal-structures|Legal structures]] · [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|Corporate actions & dividends]]

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

# Legal taxonomy of tokenized securities
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/legal-taxonomy
description: The SEC sorts tokenized stocks into a few legal types. This page explains each one, because the type decides what you actually own.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-11-18

*In plain English: The SEC sorts tokenized stocks into a few legal types. This page explains each one, because the type decides what you actually own.*

The SEC staff statement of 28 Jan 2026 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)) is the vocabulary used throughout this wiki:
- **Issuer-sponsored tokenization**: the issuer (or its agent) integrates [[concepts/glossary#dlt|DLT]] into its securityholder records; the onchain record is, or feeds, the master securityholder file. Examples: [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate Opening Bell]], [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] transfer-agent issuances.
- **Third-party tokenization**, split into:
  - **Custodial / security entitlement**: a third party holds the security and the token evidences an entitlement (e.g. UCC Article 8). Examples: Securitize Stocks, Coinbase [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]], [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] Tokenized Entitlements ([[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model|post-trade model]]). Kimber Digital Securities has described a planned token that would record a customer's security entitlement against the broker-dealer, with a matching entitlement at DTC (company release, 10 Nov 2026; the release says these capabilities are under development) ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/kimber-digital-securities-becomes-a-registered-broker-dealer-bringing-real-us-securities-onchain-302935166.html)).
  - **Synthetic / linked**: the token is a separate security (e.g. a note) or security-based swap referencing the stock. Examples: [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo Stocks]] (notes), Robinhood Stock Tokens (debt securities), bStocks (certificates).
- Format does not change legal obligations ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities); analysis: [Sidley](https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2026/01/sec-staff-unveils-a-playbook-for-tokenized-securities), [Jones Day](https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2026/02/sec-staff-provides-its-views-on-taxonomies-associated-with-tokenized-securities)).

## How must a broker-dealer hold tokenized securities?
[[concepts/glossary#rule-15c3-3|Rule 15c3-3]] possession-and-control applies to crypto asset securities. The 2020 special-purpose [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]] statement is not mandatory ([SEC TM FAQ](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-relating-crypto-asset-activities-distributed-ledger-technology)). The 17 Dec 2025 TM statement describes how a broker-dealer establishes physical possession. It covers:
- the ability to transfer the asset
- private-key protections
- network risk assessment
- contingency plans

Sources: [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers); [Sidley](https://www.sidley.com/en/insights/newsupdates/2025/12/sec-issues-further-crypto-asset-security-guidance-addresses-broker-dealer-physical-possession).

## Is a stock token a real share?

It depends on how the token is built. Some tokens *are* the share itself, recorded on the company's official register. Many widely traded tokens are not: they are a claim, certificate, note, or other instrument that references a share held somewhere else.

The SEC staff's 28 Jan 2026 statement sorts tokenized securities into issuer-sponsored tokens, where the onchain record is or feeds the issuer's official register, and third-party tokens. A third-party token may be a custodial security entitlement or a separate ("synthetic") instrument such as a note. The staff says the format does not change legal obligations, and a third-party token "may or may not confer upon the holder of the crypto asset any rights as a holder of the underlying security" ([SEC staff statement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).

IOSCO's November 2026 monitoring report draws the same line for securities regulators worldwide. It says the label "stock tokens" can cover products that "differ materially" in legal structure and investor rights, some giving only contractual or economic exposure without shareholder rights or ownership. It separates "mirroring," where the token "is merely informative with limited legal value," from cases where "the blockchain is used to record the ownership of the securities," and concludes that a product's legal and economic character "cannot be assumed from the use of tokenization alone" ([IOSCO 2026](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD832.pdf), pp. 4, 33, 50).

Examples from issuer documents, not a complete list:

- [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] are tracker certificates. They give economic exposure to the underlying equity and do not convey shareholder rights such as voting ([xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions)). Kraken's distribution FAQ puts it more strongly: holding an xStock "is not the same as buying a share of the underlying company" and does not carry voting rights or a legal claim to the company's shares or residual assets ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq), last updated 11 Nov 2026).
- [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo Stocks]] are structured notes (debt instruments) issued by a bankruptcy-remote SPV. They are designed to give economic exposure, "not direct title" to the underlying assets, and no shareholder voting, statutory information, or other shareholder rights from the underlying issuer ([Ondo legal](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory) and [overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)).
- [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase]] tokenized stocks on Base are described as a beneficial claim on a real share held in bankruptcy-remote custody, not a share recorded on the company's register ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks); see also the implementations table).
- [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens|Robinhood]] products differ by program. Jersey Stock Tokens are debt securities and give no rights in the underlying shares, as already recorded on the issuer page. EU Classic Stock Tokens are a derivatives contract with Robinhood Europe: the FAQ says "you do not own the underlying stock" and "will not have certain shareholder rights like voting" ([Classic FAQ](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)).

Issuer-sponsored tokens, where the token *is* the registered share, are listed on the implementations table. For a side-by-side of models, what a holder can redeem into, and a four-model lens, see [[comparisons/implementations-by-model]]. This is reference information, not legal advice.

See also [[comparisons/implementations-by-model|implementations compared by model]].

# Post-trade / Reg NMS-inside model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model
description: In this model a tokenized share is the same share as the normal one. It trades on the same exchanges and only the record-keeping behind it changes.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-11-12

*In plain English: In this model a tokenized share is the same share as the normal one. It trades on the same exchanges and only the record-keeping behind it changes.*

In this model the security does not change: tokenized and traditional shares share one order book, priority, CUSIP, symbol and rights, and settle through [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]]'s tokenization pilot ([SEC Nasdaq approval](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)). Components:
- **DTC Tokenized Entitlements** under the 11 Dec 2025 [[concepts/glossary#no-action-letter|no-action letter]] ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC]]).
- **Exchange rules**: [[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]] (approved 18 Mar 2026), [[platforms-venues/nyse-ice-tokenized-platform|NYSE]].
Contrast with the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|onchain-venue model]] ([[concepts/glossary#tsv|TSVs]]).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf>
- <https://www.sec.gov/files/tm/no-action/dtc-nal-121125.pdf>
- <https://www.nyse.com/publicdocs/nyse/markets/nyse/rule-filings/sec-approvals/2026/%28SR-NYSE-2026-17%29_34-105260.pdf>

# Token primitives
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/concepts/token-primitives
description: The basic technical building blocks that tokenized stocks are made of, and which projects use which.
type: concept
last_checked: 2026-11-18

*In plain English: The basic technical building blocks that tokenized stocks are made of, and which projects use which.*

The building blocks used by tokenized-stock implementations:
- **Identity-gated transfers**: [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]] (identity registry + compliance), [[standards/erc-1400|ERC-1400]] (transfer validation, partitions), [[standards/solana-token-2022|Token-2022 transfer hooks]].
- **Plain ERC-20** with offchain eligibility: Robinhood Stock Tokens are standard ERC-20s ([Robinhood](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/)). Ondo Stocks are available on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana, and some wallets show a display [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] on Solana and BNB ([Ondo overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)). The current Ondo API overview states that on-chain assets are issued as ERC-20 tokens for EVM-based chains and as SPL Token-2022 tokens on Solana ([Ondo API overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/api-reference/overview), retrieved 12 Nov 2026); the current Ondo Stocks overview and technical docs do not name the token standard.
- **[[concepts/glossary#multiplier|Multipliers]] for corporate actions**: build transactions in raw amounts, display raw x multiplier (xStocks, [docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers)); [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]] scaled UI amount; see [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]].
- **Permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|AMMs]]**: [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap v4 permissioned pools]].
- **Shared policy registries**: [[standards/b20|B20]] tokens on Base point each policy scope (transfer sender, receiver and executor, mint receiver, seize-exempt and seize receiver) at a shared Policy Registry of allowlists and blocklists, so one list update applies to every token using it. Every scope defaults to `ALWAYS_ALLOW` until it is bound. The events include `seizeWithMemo`, a deprecated freeze-style `burnBlocked`, pause, a supply cap, and bytes32 memos for reconciliation ([Base updatePolicy](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/interfaces/ib20/update-policy); [events](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/events)). That is a shared registry of lists, in contrast to [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]], where identity and compliance checks sit in the token's own registries. It also contrasts with Securitize's 12 Nov 2026 comment letter, which asks the SEC to require permissioning in the token itself rather than only in a pool allowlist, with freeze, burn and reissue as the fallback ([Securitize](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-32/4927-1134705-4042498.pdf)).

- **Official register split between chain and offchain identity**: in Invesco's IROXX fund, the Ethereum token records plus Superstate's offchain register mapping wallets to holder identity together form the official shareholder register, with allowlisted wallets, freeze, and burn and re-mint for lost keys ([IROXX prospectus](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/205007/000110465926117813/tm2627770d1_485bpos.htm); see [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]]).
- **[[concepts/glossary#oracle|Oracles]]** for a 24/5 underlying traded 24/7: [[infrastructure/chainlink-equity-feeds|Chainlink]].
- **Onchain corporate-action announcements**: a 16 Nov 2026 proposed open standard from Coinbase and [[infrastructure/broadridge|Broadridge]] (Onchain Rights) defines how a token contract can emit a structured announcement — an identifier, a short description and a URI — and link it to a JSON corporate-action document. The document format "uses corporate action vocabulary from ISO 15022 and ISO 20022, with type names from the Broadridge BRx data model." The specs "communicate the action" and "do not establish legal rights, calculate a particular holder's entitlement, determine eligibility, or submit votes and elections." As of 16 Nov 2026 the EIP texts and the canonical schema were listed as not yet published ([Onchain Rights docs](https://www.onchainrights.org/docs); [Broadridge / PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/coinbase-and-broadridge-publish-proposed-standard-for-onchain-shareholder-communications-broadridge-launches-data-oracle-302939893.html)). See [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/api-reference/overview>
- <https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers>
- <https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/interfaces/ib20/update-policy>
- <https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/events>
- <https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-32/4927-1134705-4042498.pdf>
- <https://www.onchainrights.org/docs>
- <https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/coinbase-and-broadridge-publish-proposed-standard-for-onchain-shareholder-communications-broadridge-launches-data-oracle-302939893.html>
- <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/205007/000110465926117813/tm2627770d1_485bpos.htm>

# Corporate actions & dividends
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends
description: How dividends, stock splits and votes reach you depends on how the token is built. This page compares the approaches.
last_checked: 2026-11-20

*In plain English: How dividends, stock splits and votes reach you depends on how the token is built. This page compares the approaches.*

How a dividend or split reaches a token holder depends on the model (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Multiplier (rebasing) model
[[concepts/glossary#wrapper|Wrapped]] tokens usually reinvest dividends and raise a multiplier rather than pay cash.
- **xStocks**: dividends are reinvested net of withholding; splits and reverse splits scale the multiplier ([xStocks docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/dividends-and-stock-splits)). Kraken computes the change as the net dividend (after 30% US withholding) divided by the prior close, and updates it around 8 p.m. EST the day before the ex-date ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)). Holders get no voting rights.
- **Coinbase on Base ([[standards/b20|B20]])**: cash dividends are converted to shares and reflected in the multiplier (e.g. 1.02 means one token [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeems]] for 1.02 shares). Scheduled updates give advance onchain notice via ERC-8056 ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- Robinhood also uses multipliers that reflect reinvested dividends ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary).


## Entitlement tokens
- **Securitize CETs**: a 13 Nov 2026 Securitize article says that, on supported EVM deployments, it uses display [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multipliers]] based on the ERC-8056 approach for splits, and Scaled UI Amount on [[concepts/glossary#solana|Solana]], so the economic representation can change without liquidity providers withdrawing and recreating positions. Dividends and other entitlements, in the same article, are handled by Securitize's corporate-actions processing rather than described as reinvested into the multiplier ([Securitize](https://medium.com/securitize/the-tsv-stack-you-bring-execution-and-liquidity-we-bring-the-stock-b2cb64c744ed)).

## Securitize Apple dividend (16 Nov 2026)
On 16 Nov 2026, Apple's pay date, [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]] paid Apple's \$0.27 cash dividend in USDC on Solana to holders of its Securitize Stocks Apple token. Securitize described this as its first onchain dividend on a tokenized public stock ([Carlos Domingo on X](https://x.com/carlosdomingo/status/2123822462194643349)). A Securitize payment notice states the dividend per CET as \$0.27.

Bitquery, which traced the Solana transfers (figures verified 17 Nov 2026), reported a total of \$43.14 paid in four transfers to 20 wallets, with about 93% (\$40.03) going to the market maker's inventory wallet and \$3.11 shared by 19 outside wallets. Bitquery said the amounts matched Apple's rate to the cent, that some payments were 15% or 30% short — consistent, in its reading, with US withholding on foreign holders — and that a buyer on the ex-dividend date received nothing. Apple's record date was 12 Nov 2026 ([Bitquery](https://bitquery.io/investigations/securitize-apple-dividend-onchain)).

## Issuer-sponsored and fund tokens
The token is the share, so corporate actions follow the register (Superstate). Exodus's tokens carry no economic rights of their own; those attach to the Class A share ([Exodus offering circular](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm)). WisdomTree's WTGXX accrues income daily and pays monthly in cash or [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]], or reinvests it ([WisdomTree FAQ](https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/)).

[[infrastructure/vertalo|Vertalo]], a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] in the [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]], says [[concepts/glossary#issuer-sponsored-token|issuer-sponsored tokens]] work because the shareholder records and the token agree, and that agreement drives corporate actions ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition-gains-momentum-as-qrt-vertalo-and-zerohash-join)).

## DTC
At launch, [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pays Treasury distributions in fiat to participants' traditional accounts. Equity and [[concepts/glossary#etf|ETF]] corporate actions on tokens are on the 2027+ roadmap ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)).

IOSCO's 2026 monitoring report finds that corporate actions on tokenized shares still "rely on traditional operational processes," with plans to add smart-contract features such as converting cash dividends into stablecoins or tokenized deposits; it quotes DTC's no-action materials describing that option for later versions of the service ([IOSCO 2026](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD832.pdf), p. 44).

Chainlink Labs' 11 Nov 2026 comment letter on the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] proposes principles for how a TSV should give equivalent rights effect across systems: retain verifiable evidence of issuer-notice receipt; reconcile event data across systems, including record dates, differences in finality, and transfers in progress at a cutoff, under rules approved by the party responsible for the authoritative entitlement record; and name in the Notice who maintains that record and who makes issuer communications available. Chainlink is a vendor of corporate-action infrastructure of the kind the letter discusses, and the letter is advocacy, not a Commission requirement ([Chainlink Labs](https://www.sec.gov/comments/4-927/4927-1133160-4036827.pdf)).
On 19 Nov 2026 Chainlink said UBS used the Chainlink Runtime Environment (CRE) in a production pilot to run lifecycle servicing for a tokenized structured note on Ethereum, including real-time visibility of coupon entitlements, barrier proximity and product status. This is a structured note, not a stock. Settlement using UBS digital money is described as future automation, not a live feature ([Chainlink / PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/chainlink-develops-blockchain-solution-with-ubs-for-the-2-trillion-global-structured-products-market-302944470.html)).


## A proposed open notice standard (16 Nov 2026)
On 16 Nov 2026 Coinbase and [[infrastructure/broadridge|Broadridge]] published a proposed open standard, Onchain Rights, for delivering shareholder communications (notices and corporate actions) to wallets holding tokenized shares, and said they also submitted it as an Ethereum Improvement Proposal (EIP) for review. Broadridge also launched a data oracle designed to give participating firms aggregate evidence that communications were distributed ([Broadridge / PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/coinbase-and-broadridge-publish-proposed-standard-for-onchain-shareholder-communications-broadridge-launches-data-oracle-302939893.html)). The announcement builds on Broadridge's existing ProxyVote-in-wallet work, including the 5 Nov 2026 [[issuers/dinari|Dinari]] dShares integration ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2026/broadridge-brings-proxy-voting-to-dinaris-dshares-tokenized-us-equities)).

The standard's docs describe an onchain announcement — an identifier, a short description and a link to a JSON corporate-action document — which can optionally group related token changes in the same transaction. The overview states that the specifications "communicate the action" and "do not establish legal rights, calculate a particular holder's entitlement, determine eligibility, or submit votes and elections." The document format "uses corporate action vocabulary from ISO 15022 and ISO 20022, with type names from the Broadridge BRx data model" ([Onchain Rights docs](https://www.onchainrights.org/docs)). The FAQ says the standard "announces and describes events" and "doesn't take votes or move money"; "Onchain voting is the next phase" ([Onchain Rights](https://www.onchainrights.org/)). As of 16 Nov 2026, the project's EIP References page lists both "Onchain Announcements" and "Corporate Action Announcement Content" as "Coming soon," and the canonical JSON schema is marked "Publication pending" ([EIP References](https://www.onchainrights.org/docs/specs/eip-references); [JSON Schema](https://www.onchainrights.org/docs/specs/json-schema)).

This is a communications layer, not an entitlement engine. It sits alongside, rather than replacing, the reconciliation questions in Chainlink Labs' 11 Nov 2026 letter ([Chainlink Labs](https://www.sec.gov/comments/4-927/4927-1133160-4036827.pdf)), which asked how a TSV should retain evidence of issuer-notice receipt, reconcile record dates and transfers in progress, and name who maintains the authoritative entitlement record. Implementation of the Coinbase and Broadridge standard "will depend on the applicable share structure, intermediaries and legal requirements" ([Broadridge / PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/coinbase-and-broadridge-publish-proposed-standard-for-onchain-shareholder-communications-broadridge-launches-data-oracle-302939893.html)). See also [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase tokenized stocks]] and [[concepts/token-primitives|token primitives]].

## What this means for holders
- Wrapped tokens often reflect dividends and splits through a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] instead of cash; native shares and DTC-based tokens follow the normal share's corporate actions.
- Voting rights usually stay with the [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] or issuer for wrapped tokens; check each issuer page.
- A 16 Nov 2026 proposed standard aims to deliver the same structured shareholder notice to any wallet, broker or custodian that can read it; the standard itself does not create legal rights, calculate a holder's entitlement, or submit votes ([Onchain Rights docs](https://www.onchainrights.org/docs)).
- Where a field says `unknown`, the sources so far do not say how that issuer handles it.

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

## Sources

# Custody
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/custody
description: Who holds the real share, and who controls the token, differs by model. This page shows who keeps what.
last_checked: 2026-11-13

*In plain English: Who holds the real share, and who controls the token, differs by model. This page shows who keeps what.*

Who holds the real share, and who holds the keys, differs by model (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Who holds the shares behind most tokens

For tokens that are claims on real shares, those shares sit with a custodian or broker-dealer named in that product's documents — or, in some cases, the documents only say a regulated custodian and do not name the firm. Alpaca is named below only where a document retrieved for this update says so. Issuer-sponsored tokens do not use this pattern: the transfer agent keeps the company's register.

| Issuer or product | Who holds the backing shares, per the documents | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase]] tokenized stocks | Alpaca, in a bankruptcy-remote structure | Already recorded on the issuer page from Coinbase/Base and Alpaca ITN sources. |
| [[issuers/ondo-global-markets\|Ondo Stocks]] | A regulated custodial broker-dealer, not named on the legal page; Ankura Trust Company acts as security agent | The legal page says the notes are backed 1:1 (plus a buffer) by underlying securities "held via a regulated custodial broker-dealer (and cash in transit)" ([Ondo legal](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)). Alpaca Markets appears on Ondo's partner list; that list is not, by itself, a statement that Alpaca is the custodian of the backing shares. |
| [[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]] | Company statements differ | Kraken's FAQ, last updated 11 Nov 2026, says underlying shares are held by Alpaca Securities LLC, with InCore Bank as a secondary custodian ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)). The official xStocks FAQ still says "regulated custodians" without naming them ([xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions)). Payward's 11 Nov 2026 release says GTN handles global execution and custody of the traditional assets that underpin each token, in the context of a Payward Services partnership ([Payward](https://www.payward.com/press-release/xstocks-uk-eu-equities)). These statements are recorded side by side, not reconciled here. |
| [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood]] | A US-based custody partner or US-licensed institution, not named in the documents cited here | Jersey Stock Tokens: "US-based custody partner (name: unknown)," already on the issuer page. EU Classic Stock Tokens: "The underlying assets are held securely by a US-licensed institution," unnamed ([Classic FAQ](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)). |
| [[issuers/backpack\|Backpack Securities]] | RQD Clearing, LLC and Atomic Vault Securities, LLC | Already recorded on the issuer page. |
| [[issuers/dinari\|Dinari]] | Qualified custody, firm not named on the issuer page | Already recorded; this pass did not find a named custodian in newly retrieved issuer docs. |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize]] Stocks | RQD Clearing has been described as having a role in clearing, custody and settlement | That wording is already on the issuer page, attributed to CoinDesk via an RQD repost, not to a Securitize prospectus retrieved here. |
| [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell\|Superstate]] / issuer-sponsored shares | Not a third-party custodian of a wrapper | The token is the entry on the company's transfer-agent register. |

Third-party market-share figures that attribute most backing shares to a single broker were not included: a RWA Foundation or Token Terminal percentage was not verified against a methodology write-up in this pass.

In a 15 Oct 2026 interview on NYSE Live, Alpaca's co-founder and CEO, Yoshi Yokokawa — not NYSE staff — described the firm as providing traditional-finance clearing and custody of the underlying stocks that are minted into tokens, and cited a clearing-broker license and DTC membership as part of that role. That is Alpaca's own description, from auto-generated captions of the interview, not a substitute for the product documents in the table above ([NYSE Live](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c8VAgn88uqs)).

## Backed (third-party) models
Backed models hold the underlying shares with a [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] or broker-dealer ([[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]]: US broker-dealers; Dinari: registered US broker-dealer; Coinbase: bankruptcy-remote structure) ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary; [Fensory](https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms), secondary). SEC staff note that holders of third-party tokens may face risks, such as the third party's bankruptcy, that holders of the underlying share would not ([SEC staff statement, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).

## Issuer-sponsored models
These replace custody with a transfer-agent register: the token is the ownership record (see [[issuers/securitize|Securitize]], [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]]).

Where that register, or a component of it, sits on a public chain the transfer agent does not control, recordkeeping controls become a custody issue as well as a regulatory one. Metrika's 3 Nov 2026 comment letter on the SEC transfer agent proposal (File S7-2026-30) is advocacy, not law; it asks the SEC to treat network risk as a material risk under Rule 17ad-12, to treat exclusive control as covering the token's privileged functions and the off-chain address-to-holder mapping, to treat an item as posted when it reaches the agent's documented finality standard, and to reconcile supply across networks against the control book ([Metrika letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-30/s7202630-1119921-3984266.pdf)). The incident figures in that letter are Metrika's monitoring data.

## DTC tokenized entitlements
Tokens are backed 1:1 by securities held at [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]], and DTC keeps the official books and records ([[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTCC Tokenization Service]]; [DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)). The service went live on 28 Oct 2026, delivering tokens to participants' wallets of choice ([DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)).

## Broker-dealer custody of tokens
SEC staff will not object to a broker-dealer treating itself as having "physical possession" of a crypto asset security under Rule 15c3-3(b)(1) if conditions are met, chiefly control of the private keys and safeguards against their theft or loss ([SEC staff statement, 17 Dec 2025](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/trading-markets-121725-statement-custody-crypto-asset-securities-broker-dealers)). This is a staff statement, not a rule.

## Vendors
[[infrastructure/zerohash|Zerohash]] markets a tokenization engine to brokerages ([Zerohash](https://zerohash.com/industries/brokerages)).

## What this means for holders
- With a [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapper]], your protection depends on the issuer's [[concepts/glossary#custodian|custodian]] and whether the structure is [[concepts/glossary#bankruptcy-remote|bankruptcy-remote]].
- Platform custody and token custody are separate questions: a venue can list a token without holding it (e.g. [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE]]).

## What if the issuer, custodian or my wallet has a problem?

It depends on the structure, and the product documents are the source, not this page. This is reference information, not legal advice or a prediction of what would happen in a default.

- **Issuer-sponsored tokens.** The token is the entry on the company's official register. A lost key may be recoverable if the transfer agent can re-verify the holder, as already described for the Fairmint / CNTN example on the [[build/trading-reference-architecture#issuer-sponsored-register-permissions-and-recovery|reference architecture]].
- **Bankruptcy-remote wrappers.** Some third-party products describe a bankruptcy-remote SPV, segregated custody, and a security agent. The official xStocks FAQ describes collateral in segregated accounts under a three-party structure (issuer, custodians, and an independent security agent) and says that if the issuer defaults, the security agent may assume control and distribute proceeds per the prospectus ([xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions)). Ondo describes a bankruptcy-remote SPV, overcollateralization, a first-priority security interest held by a third-party security agent, and daily attestations ([Ondo overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview) and [legal](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)). Kraken's FAQ says the SPV structure is designed so that if Kraken or Backed goes bankrupt, users can still claim the underlying value of their assets directly with Alpaca ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)). Those are the firms' descriptions.
- **Staff risk note.** SEC staff have said that holders of third-party tokens "may be exposed to risks with respect to the third party, such as bankruptcy, to which a holder of the underlying security would not necessarily be exposed" ([SEC staff statement, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).
- **Issuer freeze or blocking powers, only where documented.** Coinbase's B20 docs say policies can allowlist or block transfers (a blocked transfer reverts), that specific contract functions can be paused, and that a Coinbase onchain oracle registry can pause a feed so that it holds the last known value; mint and redeem can also be paused offchain during a corporate action without pausing the token onchain ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). This page does not attribute a general freeze power to issuers whose documents are not cited for it.
- **Wallet or venue problems.** If you hold the token in a self-custodial wallet, control of the wallet is separate from who holds the backing shares. A venue can list a token without holding it. Recovery after a lost or compromised wallet depends on the product: an issuer-sponsored transfer agent may have a documented recovery path; a freely transferable wrapper may not.

*Reference information only, not investment advice. This page is not a prediction of recovery in a default.*

# Legal structures
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/legal-structures
description: Tokenized stocks come in a few legal forms. Some are the real share; others are a claim or a note that tracks it.
last_checked: 2026-11-20

*In plain English: Tokenized stocks come in a few legal forms. Some are the real share; others are a claim or a note that tracks it.*

Tokenized stocks fall into distinct legal models ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/)):
- **Debt security / certificate** backed by shares (Robinhood, bStocks, xStocks).
- **Beneficial claim** on custodied shares (Coinbase [[concepts/glossary#b20|B20]]; Securitize Stocks as [[concepts/glossary#security-entitlement|security entitlements]], convertible to registered shares).
- **Issuer-sponsored shares** recorded by a [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] (Securitize, Superstate Opening Bell).
- **Blockchain-native equity** (Figure FGRS).
- **Same security, tokenized form** inside the US market structure (Nasdaq / [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pilot, [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)).
Rights differ: backing does not automatically confer shareholder rights. In the UK, an 18 Nov 2026 letter from the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion says "the treatment of registers in the Companies Act... could prevent the issuance of digitally native equities" ([letter](https://www.theglobalcity.uk/PositiveWebsite/media/research-downloads/20261118_CW-Letter.pdf)).

In the [[concepts/glossary#issuer-sponsored-token|issuer-sponsored]] model the token is tied to the company's official shareholder register, so voting, dividend and corporate-action rights carry over; wrapped and synthetic tokens only track the share. Most US shares sit in [[concepts/glossary#street-name|street name]], registered to DTC's nominee [[concepts/glossary#cede--co|Cede & Co.]]; moving them into the holder's own name runs through the [[concepts/glossary#direct-registration-system-drs|Direct Registration System (DRS)]], which DTC has proposed to speed up "from days to minutes" ([SEC notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20301/self-regulatory-organizations-the-depository-trust-company-notice-of-filing-of-proposed-rule-change)). Since Sep 2026 the [[concepts/issuer-sponsored-token-coalition|Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition]] has pushed this model ([Bullish](https://www.bullish.com/us/news-insights/leading-market-infrastructure-firms-form-coalition-to-advance-issuer-sponsored-tokenized-securities)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.theglobalcity.uk/PositiveWebsite/media/research-downloads/20261118_CW-Letter.pdf>

# Regulation
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/regulation
description: The main US and international rule changes for tokenized securities, in date order.
last_checked: 2026-11-20

*In plain English: The main US and international rule changes for tokenized securities, in date order.*

Key US milestones: [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] [[concepts/glossary#no-action-letter|no-action letter]] (11 Dec 2025) and SEC approval of Nasdaq's tokenized trading rule (18 Mar 2026) ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)); WisdomTree's [[concepts/glossary#exemptive-relief|exemptive relief]] for 24/7 fund-share trading (Feb 2026, [WisdomTree](https://ir.wisdomtree.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/777/wisdomtree-to-launch-247-trading-and-instant-settlement)). Non-US issuers sit in Jersey, BVI and ADGM ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/)).

Earlier input: at a 27 Jan 2026 SEC Crypto Task Force meeting, SIFMA (with Citadel and JPMorgan) argued for rulemaking over broad exemptions and split tokenized securities into three models: native (issued by the issuer and its [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]]), wrapped (an ADR-like token that is a separate security) and security entitlement tokens (a custodian's record of a customer's holding) ([SEC memo](https://www.sec.gov/files/ctf-memo-sifma-cahill-gordon-reindel-llp-citadel-llc-jpmorgan-chase-co-012726.pdf)).

Recent changes (Sep to Oct 2026): the SEC's [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] for tokenized NMS stock (17 Sep 2026, [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-90-sec-issues-innovation-exemption-facilitate-trading-tokenized-nms-stock-request-comment)), which Better Markets' 22 Oct comment letter urges the SEC to withdraw in favor of notice-and-comment rulemaking ([Better Markets](https://bettermarkets.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Better-Markets-Comment-Letter-SEC-Innovation-Exemption.pdf)), while SIFMA's 19 Oct letter asks for amendments such as issuer opt-in consent and a 90-day objection period ([SIFMA](https://www.sifma.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SIFMA-Innovation-Exemption-Initial-Letter-10-19-2026.pdf)), Solana Policy Institute's 22 Oct letter backs the order and asks the SEC to define "public, permissionless" ledgers by who controls them ([Solana Policy Institute](https://www.sec.gov/comments/4-927/4927-1106380-3893468.pdf)), and Malinova and Park (23 Oct) argue the volume caps block arbitrage and raise trading costs ([Malinova and Park](https://www.sec.gov/comments/4-927/4927-1107499-3908312.pdf)); Shadow SEC Statement No. 17, filed 10 Nov 2026 (statement dated 19 Oct) by five securities-law scholars including former SEC General Counsel John C. Coates, argues that the order is a legislative rule in substance that should have gone through APA notice and comment, and that it will fragment liquidity because it does not require connectivity between TSVs or aggregation of quotes or last-sale information ([Shadow SEC Statement No. 17](https://www.sec.gov/comments/4-927/4927-1131060-4029687.pdf)); CFTC staff FAQs on tokenized permitted investments (24 Sep 2026, [CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9303-26)); the OCC's final GENIUS Act rule, effective 18 Jan 2027 (21 Oct 2026, [OCC](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html)); the FCA and Bank of England feedback statement FS26/1 (14 Sep 2026, [FCA](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/feedback-statements/fs26-1-tokenisation-wholesale-markets)); and EU Council agreement on key elements of the market integration package, which would widen the DLT Pilot Regime (9 Oct 2026, [Council](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/10/09/savings-and-investments-union-council-agrees-key-elements-of-crucial-measures-to-deepen-eu-capital-markets/)).

November 2026 signals: IOSCO's 2026 monitoring report calls tokenization "transitional and fragmented" and asks regulators to tell tokenized shares that carry shareholder rights apart from products that only give price exposure ([IOSCO 2026](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD832.pdf)). Four Senate Democrats (Alsobrooks, Warner, Gallego and Cortez Masto) wrote to Chairman Atkins on 13 Nov 2026 asking 13 questions about the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]], including AML/KYC, token-level transfer restrictions and issuer opt-outs, and urging notice-and-comment rulemaking ([letter](https://www.alsobrooks.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Alsobrooks_Warner_Cortez_Masto_Gallego_SEC_Innovation_Exemption_Tokenization_Letter_11-12-2026_@_02-10_PM.pdf)). On 16 Nov 2026 SEC Trading and Markets Director Jamie Selway, speaking for himself, said a permanent rule proposal has "got to be a 2027 event" ([Unchained livestream at 1:10:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwAidpXpJJ4&t=4255s)). Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on 17 Nov 2026 that atomic settlement should not be the only model for tokenized markets ([Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/waller20261117a.htm); see [[topics/settlement-and-matching|Settlement & matching]]). On the derivatives side, the CFTC set a 15 Dec 2026 roundtable on 24/7 trading whose agenda asks how tokenization and stablecoins could address roadblocks to 24/7 clearing ([CFTC](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9327-26); [agenda](https://www.cftc.gov/media/14941/RoundtablePublicFacing_Agenda121526/download)).

Transfer agent rules (proposed, Sep 2026): the SEC proposed amendments to its transfer agent rules (Release 34-106246, 1 Sep 2026, 91 FR 56946, File S7-2026-30), as cited in [Nasdaq's comment letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-30/s7202630-1122619-3995826.pdf). Comment letters are advocacy, not law, and they diverge: Nasdaq (5 Nov) asks for interoperability between onchain and offchain master securityholder files and the national clearance and settlement system, and fungibility at the recordkeeping layer ([Nasdaq](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-30/s7202630-1122619-3995826.pdf)); Coinbase (3 Nov) asks that holders be identifiable by wallet address without a mandatory name and mailing address, and that a blockchain record can be the master file ([Coinbase](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-30/s7202630-1119719-3983946.pdf)); [[infrastructure/fairmint|Fairmint]] (3 Nov) proposes one recordkeeping transfer agent with co-transfer agents per venue and a functional test of "exclusive control" ([Fairmint](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-30/s7202630-1120639-3987647.pdf)); Metrika (3 Nov) addresses keeping the master securityholder file on a public chain the transfer agent does not control, and asks the SEC to treat network risk as a material risk under Rule 17ad-12 calling for real-time monitoring, to treat exclusive control as covering the token's privileged functions (issue, cancel, freeze, force-transfer) and the off-chain address-to-holder mapping, to treat an item as posted when it reaches finality under the agent's documented standard, and to have Form TA-2 name the networks used ([Metrika letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-30/s7202630-1119921-3984266.pdf)). The network-incident figures in that letter, including a 12 Aug 2026 Solana finality stall (roughly 29 percent of staked SOL offline; no blocks finalized for roughly half an hour) and five Solana protocol changes between 21 Aug and 21 Oct 2026, are Metrika's monitoring data. An official onchain register is already possible today (for example CNTN's); the name and mailing address baseline is the proposal's. Other letters, including from the Blockchain Association and the Crypto Council for Innovation, which Coinbase endorses, are on the [SEC comment page](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/public-comments/s7-2026-30). Detail: [[build/trading-reference-architecture#holder-rights-and-compliance-controls|Holder rights and compliance controls]].

Country-by-country status: [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].

Outside the US (Sep to Nov 2026): South Korea published its tokenization roadmap (4 Sep 2026, [FSC](https://fsc.go.kr/eng/pr010101/87653)) and draft rules for the regime that starts 4 Feb 2027, with comments open to 11 Nov 2026 ([FSC](https://fsc.go.kr/eng/pr010101/87834)); the Reserve Bank of Australia consulted on settling tokenised assets in central bank money (3 Sep 2026, [RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/tokenised-money/the-role-of-rits-in-supporting-settlement-in-a-tokenised-ecosystem/pdf/the-role-of-rits-in-supporting-settlement-in-a-tokenised-ecosystem.pdf)). In the UK, on 18 Nov 2026 the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion welcomed an enabling amendment the government had laid to the Financial Services and Markets Bill, and said settlement finality and Companies Act register rules still need greater certainty before digitally native equities can be issued ([letter](https://www.theglobalcity.uk/PositiveWebsite/media/research-downloads/20261118_CW-Letter.pdf)). See [[concepts/international|International regimes]].

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.theglobalcity.uk/PositiveWebsite/media/research-downloads/20261118_CW-Letter.pdf>
