# Settlement & matching
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/settlement-and-matching
description: How tokenized stock trades get matched and settled, and how that differs from today's next-day settlement.
last_checked: 2026-11-18

*In plain English: How tokenized stock trades get matched and settled, and how that differs from today's next-day settlement.*

Tokenized stocks trade and settle in several ways (see [[overview|the overview]]).

## Where do tokenized stocks trade?
On centralized exchanges, onchain DEXs, permissioned Tokenized Securities Venues, ATSs and national exchanges, each with a different settlement model.
- **Centralized exchanges** list tokens: Kraken trades most xStocks 24/5, with 10 trading 24/7 on Kraken Pro; withdrawn tokens can trade 24/7 on DEXs ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)).
- **Onchain DEXs**: [[concepts/glossary#wrapper|wrapped]] tokens trade permissionlessly in DeFi pools.
- **Tokenized Securities Venues** run permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker|AMM]] pools under the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]]. Conditions include symbol and volume caps, a 30-day issuer objection window, and trading halts in step with the primary market ([SEC order 34-106402](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)). See [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE TSV]] and [[infrastructure/uniswap-permissioned-pools|Uniswap permissioned pools]].
- **[[concepts/glossary#ats|ATS]]**: Figure's blockchain stock settles on Provenance in YLDS ([Figure 424(b)(4)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2064124/000162828026008786/figure-blockchain424b4.htm)); see [[issuers/figure-open|Figure OPEN]].
- **National exchanges** trade tokenized and traditional shares on one order book with equal priority, settled through [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] ([[platforms-venues/nasdaq-tokenized-securities|Nasdaq]]; [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/nasdaq/2026/34-105047.pdf)).

## Post-trade
DTC's Tokenization Service went live on 28 Oct 2026 with 20 signed participants ([DTCC](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-goes-live)). It converts book-entry positions into tokens and back, targeting 15 minutes or less ([DTCC tear sheet](https://dtcclearning.com/documents/dtcc-digital-assets/digital-asset-solutions/tokenization-service/5699-dtcc-tokenization-service-product-tear-sheet-and-high-level-roadmap/file.html)). DTC's participant notice says conversion orders run Monday to Friday, 2 a.m.-6 p.m. ET, and tokens then move 24/7 between allowed listed [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] on supported networks ([DTC notice DAS-001](https://files.dtcc.com/download/assets/DAS-001/8a31d732d2d311f1a30ef632b7f70f6d)). On-chain netting and digital cash are on the 2027+ roadmap.

The first named trading and financing stack on top of DTC's tokens was announced on 17 Nov 2026: Talos quotes over its RFQ network, Marex finances as prime broker, and [[infrastructure/broadridge|Broadridge]]'s DLX orchestrates atomic onchain settlement while keeping books and records in sync. It starts with financing tokenized U.S. Treasuries outside market hours and has no stated go-live date ([Broadridge](https://www.broadridge.com/press-release/2026/broadridge-to-enable-institutional-trading-of-dtcc-tokenized-securities)).

In Europe, the ESM settled a €1bn DLT bond through the Eurosystem's Pontes platform on 26 Oct 2026, with the bond on Clearstream's D7 and the cash leg in central bank money in T2 ([Deutsche Börse release](https://www.deutsche-boerse.com/dbg-en/media/news-stories/press-releases/ESM-is-first-European-supranational-issuer-to-settle-DLT-based-bond-issuance-on-Eurosystem-s-Pontes-platform-with-Bundesbank-and-Clearstream-5660764)).

On 16 Nov 2026 DBS and Kinexys by J.P. Morgan launched a commercially ready interoperability solution for instant USD transfers between blockchain-based accounts in the United States and Singapore, including on weekends. This is the cash leg, not a tokenized security: it connects DBS Token Services with Kinexys's account-based permissioned [[concepts/glossary#tokenized-deposit|tokenized-deposit]] network (its Blockchain Deposit Account network). The DBS release says the solution "leverages Partior for settlement orchestration," and that the two banks "are founding shareholders of Partior, a global distributed ledger technology market infrastructure for clearing and settlement." Ant International is the inaugural client. The launch operationalises an interoperability framework the two banks announced in November 2025. Transfers on the Kinexys Blockchain Deposit Account network are described as 24/7/365 and same-day; moving funds between traditional demand-deposit accounts and Blockchain Deposit Accounts still has a three-hour downtime every Saturday from 3–6 p.m. ET, with an enhancement under development ([DBS release](https://www.dbs.com/newsroom/DBS_and_Kinexys_by_JP_Morgan_launch_industry_first_247_interoperability_solution_for_cross_border_tokenised_deposit_transfers)).

On 16 Nov 2026 Zelle demonstrated a confidential transfer of $1.25 million in ZelleUSD (ZLUSD) on stage at Solana Breakpoint, between demo banks labeled Bank Alpha and Bank Beta. The official @solana video of the demo is marked "Solana devnet" and describes "an encrypted transfer where the amount is hidden from the public chain." This is a [[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|stablecoin]] cash-leg example, not a tokenized deposit or a tokenized security. Anchorage Digital's ZLUSD attestation page states that "ZLUSD is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued for Zelle® by Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A., redeemable 1:1 for U.S. Dollars and designed for payments, transfers, and conversions." Anchorage's 30 Sep 2026 ZLUSD Reserve Report records total ZLUSD redeemable tokens outstanding of 85,151 and states that "Blockchain Solana refers to the smart contract running on Solana at 7NNkMtGACBbwJdMRYD2KchTKm2xBwnsb4bT7YSfRUWZ4." Early Warning Services, the network operator of Zelle, unveiled ZelleUSD on 11 June 2026 to "support future international payment capabilities in other markets." In the same release it said India would be the first country where U.S. consumers can use Zelle to send money overseas, and that "Initial availability is expected before the end of this year." That release does not say the India corridor uses ZelleUSD, and no consumer or mainnet launch date has been given ([Zelle release](https://www.zelle.com/press-releases/zelle-heads-to-india-unveils-zelleusdsm-stablecoin-other-markets), [Anchorage ZLUSD attestations](https://www.anchorage.com/platform/zlusd-reserve-attestations), [30 Sep 2026 ZLUSD Reserve Report](https://learn.anchorage.com/09.30.26_ZLUSD-Stablecoin-Attestation-Report-signed.pdf), [@solana](https://x.com/solana/status/2122284580405236216)).

Atomic settlement is not the only model regulators expect. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on 17 Nov 2026 that market participants "cautioned against viewing it as the only settlement model for tokenized markets," and that "net settlement and batch settlement, where only net amounts need to be funded, will remain useful when saving liquidity is a priority, as in high-volume capital market activity." He also said central bank money "need not be used in every transaction," but its presence at the foundation is essential, and that assets moving across networks "must maintain legal identity, ownership rights, economic terms, compliance obligations, corporate-action treatment, and access to liquidity" ([Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/waller20261117a.htm)).

On the cash leg, a 16 Nov 2026 SIFMA and Deloitte white paper built from discussions with 17 institutions says the question for payment stablecoins and tokenized deposits "is not which would 'win,'" but where each fits. It names atomic [[concepts/glossary#dvp|DvP]], intraday repo, collateral mobility, margining and corporate-action processing as near-term uses, and lists open needs: interoperability, standards, and regulatory treatment such as HQLA eligibility and accounting. Participants disagreed on whether a defined "settlement day" survives in a 24/7 market ([SIFMA and Deloitte](https://www.sifma.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Digital-Cash-White-Paper-SIFMA-and-Deloitte.pdf)). This is an industry view, not regulation.

Cross-ledger atomic settlement without a shared ledger has been tested between central banks. In Project Simbolon (16 Nov 2026), the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Deutsche Bundesbank, with DBS, Deutsche Bank and Partior, ran euro/Singapore-dollar payment-versus-payment across their two wholesale CBDC test ledgers. Tokens were locked in escrow on both ledgers; zero-knowledge proofs showed each lock was final; then "a single settlement decision was recorded and proven to each ledger," releasing both. The note says proof generation took most of the settlement time and that legal finality still depends on each central bank's rules. It is a proof of concept in test environments ([MAS insights note](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/development/fintech/project-simbolon/project-simbolon-insights-note.pdf); [MAS release](https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2026/mas-and-deutsche-bundesbank-advance-cross-border-digital-asset-settlement-connectivity)).

Central banks are weighing how to link token platforms to their payment systems. The Reserve Bank of Australia's Sep 2026 consultation lays out three [[concepts/glossary#dvp|DvP]] models: lock the asset, then pay in the central bank system (used by Australia's Austraclear and CHESS today); lock the central bank money, then move the asset (used in property settlement); or lock both through a synchronisation operator (as the Bank of England and Bundesbank have considered). It picks none ([RBA consultation paper](https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/tokenised-money/the-role-of-rits-in-supporting-settlement-in-a-tokenised-ecosystem/pdf/the-role-of-rits-in-supporting-settlement-in-a-tokenised-ecosystem.pdf)).

## Can tokenized assets be used as collateral at a clearing house?
The Bank of England's 29 Oct 2026 consultation says UK [[concepts/glossary#ccp|CCPs]] can already accept tokenised forms of eligible collateral (cash, bonds and other instruments, gold) under existing rules. Its draft expectations cover liquidity, valuation and interoperability, settlement finality, credit and concentration risk, operational resilience, and custody. Liquidity must be judged separately from the underlying asset, since trading hours and conversion can affect a forced sale. It also asks about wider collateral such as stablecoins and tokenised money market funds. Closes 12 Feb 2027 ([Bank of England CP](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/paper/2026/cp/supervisory-expectations-for-ccps-seeking-to-accept-tokenised-collateral)).

## How liquid are tokenized stocks?
Coinbase Institutional's research team noted that tokenized-stock order books remain thin, with [[concepts/glossary#slippage|slippage]] and volatility significantly higher than in the underlying equity, especially post-market or under stress. It also flagged [[concepts/glossary#oracle|oracle]] errors or lags as a risk to token/collateral equivalence ([Coinbase Institutional](https://www.coinbase.com/institutional/research-insights/research/market-intelligence/major-trends-in-tokenization), 10 Jan 2026).

## What prices a stock token when the market is closed?

There is no single official off-hours price. Secondary-market prices are whatever buyers and sellers agree, including when the cash market is shut. Official oracles and issuer mint/redeem windows often follow the underlying market's sessions and can go stale, pause, or use a different method off-hours.

- **Oracle market-status flags.** For traditional-market assets, Chainlink Data Streams include a `marketStatus` flag in price reports and tell developers to treat that flag, not the report's timestamps, as the signal for whether the market is open. The flag "is provided for referential purposes only," and developers must assess market status themselves. On 24/5 US Equities streams the values (Eastern Time) are: 0 Unknown; 1 Pre-market (4:00am–9:30am Monday–Friday); 2 Regular hours (9:30am–4:00pm); 3 Post-market (4:00pm–8:00pm); 4 Overnight (8:00pm–4:00am Sunday evening–Friday morning); 5 Closed (weekends, holidays, or unexpected closures; about 8:00pm Friday–8:00pm Sunday). 24/7 US Equities streams keep updating while `marketStatus` is 5, switching to an off-hours price derived from perpetual futures markets ([Chainlink Data Streams](https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/rwa-streams/24-5-us-equities-user-guide)).
- **Staleness and pauses.** Chainlink also tells developers to implement staleness checks for when reports stop arriving. Coinbase tokenized-equity feeds on Base "run 24/5, hold the last close on weekends and holidays, and freeze during corporate actions." Off-hours, `updatedAt` stops advancing while the contract stays callable. The Base docs say: "Always read `updatedAt` and apply staleness bounds before relying on the price; never settle or liquidate against a frozen feed." A Coinbase onchain oracle registry can also pause a feed so it holds the last known value ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- **Issuer mint and redeem windows.** xStocks issuance and redemption by minters and redeemers "are limited to business days when the US market is open, normally 24/5," while tokens "can be traded on secondary markets 24/7" ([xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions)). Ondo's platform is generally open 8:05pm ET Sunday through 7:59pm ET Friday, in Pre-Market, Core, Post-Market and Overnight sessions, with a separate Off-Hours session for weekends, holidays and early-close days on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana. As of a 16 Nov 2026 snapshot, 32 assets were enabled; buys and sells are still quoted, minted and redeemed instantly, each asset has its own dynamic Off-Hours limit, and quotes can be declined at the limit ([Ondo Off-Hours](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/off-hours-trading)). Off-Hours quotes use the same proprietary method, "bid-ask spreads can be wider," size is subject to conservative limits, and "the price of a token may diverge more significantly from the value the underlying security will have when its primary market next reopens" ([Ondo market hours](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/market-hours-and-trading-availability) and [pricing](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/token-and-quote-pricing)). Ondo's 27 Oct 2026 blog, already cited on the Robinhood issuer page, notes that a Stock Token mint/redeem window can close while onchain trading continues, which can open a price gap ([Ondo](https://ondo.finance/blog/ondo-stocks-live-on-robinhood-chain-and-uniswap)).
- **Collateral liquidation when the underlying is closed.** Lending markets can still liquidate a position while the cash equity market is shut. Kamino's isolated Backpack Market was described, in a 4 Nov 2026 Business Wire release already on the Backpack page, as carrying liquidation risk even when the underlying market is closed ([Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261104930970/en/Kamino-and-Backpack-Securities-Expand-Credit-for-Tokenized-U.S.-Equities)). The Base docs' warning not to settle or liquidate against a frozen feed is the vendor's guidance for integrators, not a statement that every protocol follows it ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- **How much trading happens off-hours.** The IMF's October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report found that more than 50% of trading in a sample of tokenized equities occurred outside regular US market hours ([IMF GFSR Oct 2026, ch. 3](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/gfsr/2026/october/english/ch3.pdf)). That is context for why off-hours pricing matters, not a pricing method.

See also the off-hours oracle and collateral pattern on the [[build/trading-reference-architecture#off-hours-pricing-and-collateral|reference architecture]].

# Who can buy
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/topics/who-can-buy
description: Whether you can buy a given stock token depends on where you live and how the token is structured.
last_checked: 2026-11-18

*In plain English: Whether you can buy a given stock token depends on where you live and how the token is structured.*

Who can hold a tokenized stock depends on the structure (see [[overview|the overview]] and [[topics/legal-structures|legal structures]]).

## Can US persons buy offshore wrapped tokens?
Most offshore products exclude US persons ([[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]], [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]], Coinbase, Robinhood) ([Zerion](https://zerion.io/blog/best-tokenized-stock-platforms/), secondary; [Fensory](https://fensory.com/best/tokenized-stocks-platforms), secondary). [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] are offered to eligible non-US clients in 110+ countries and are not available in the US, Canada, the UK or Australia ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq)).

In a 16 Nov 2026 livestream, SEC Trading and Markets Director Jamie Selway, speaking for himself, said US investors accessing synthetic stock tokens on offshore venues is "not compliant" and that action could be taken ([Unchained livestream at 1:04:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwAidpXpJJ4&t=3851s)). Separately, four senators' 13 Nov 2026 letter notes that the Innovation Exemption permissions access to trading but does not require token-level transfer restrictions, so a token bought by a verified buyer could later move to an unverified wallet ([letter](https://www.alsobrooks.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Alsobrooks_Warner_Cortez_Masto_Gallego_SEC_Innovation_Exemption_Tokenization_Letter_11-12-2026_@_02-10_PM.pdf); see [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]]).

**Market size estimates.** Blockchain data firm Bitquery estimates \$3.2B of tokenized stocks from six large issuers were held outside issuer wallets on 31 Oct 2026, up from \$585M at end-2025. Binance's bStocks were about 41% (\$1.31B), most of it in Binance's own wallets; excluding exchange wallets, [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]] led at \$848M. Counting tokens minted but not sold would give \$48.7B, which Bitquery excludes. This is Bitquery's on-chain estimate, not an issuer or regulator figure ([Bitquery](https://bitquery.io/investigations/tokenized-stocks-market-size)).

IOSCO's 2026 monitoring report, citing RWA.xyz, puts tokenized equities and equity-linked products at \$1.7B on 30 Jun 2026, up from \$330M on 1 Jul 2025, with Ondo and xStocks the two largest platforms ([IOSCO 2026](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD832.pdf), p. 34). Different trackers count different products, so these figures are not directly comparable.

Separately, in a 15 Oct 2026 interview on NYSE Live, Alpaca's co-founder and CEO, Yoshi Yokokawa, put US equities tokenized as SPV-wrapped tokens at about \$3.5B, against an approximately \$86T US equity market cap, which he said was less than one basis point. That is his estimate as of mid-October 2026, quoted from auto-generated captions of the interview, not a verified market figure, and it is a different scope and date from Bitquery's 31 Oct estimate. Yokokawa is Alpaca's CEO, not NYSE staff ([NYSE Live](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c8VAgn88uqs)).


## Does being able to open an app or a website mean I am eligible?

No. Being able to reach a site, an app, or an onchain pool — including through a VPN — does not confer eligibility. Issuer terms still restrict who may buy or hold the token.

- [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] are "not marketed, offered, or solicited in the United States" ([xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions)). Kraken's FAQ says they "are not accessible in the US (or to US persons), Canada, UK, or Australia" ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq), last updated 11 Nov 2026).
- [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo Stocks]] are offered only under Regulation S to persons located outside the United States who are not "US persons" as defined in Rule 902, are not acting for the account or benefit of any US person, and are not originating a buy order in the United States. The tokens may not be resold to any US person or into the United States unless a registration or exemption applies and the Sales Terms are followed ([Ondo legal](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)).
- Coinbase tokenized stocks "are only available to persons in eligible jurisdictions outside of the U.S." ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens|Robinhood Stock Tokens]] are recorded on the issuer page as not offered to US persons, with further country exclusions listed there from the issuer's documents.

This is reference information about those published terms, not legal advice, and not a description of how to get around them.

## How can US investors buy tokenized stocks?
Through a US broker-dealer, through issuer-sponsored shares behind KYC and a transfer-agent whitelist, or as an approved participant on a permissioned Tokenized Securities Venue.
- [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|Broker-dealer]] model: [[issuers/dinari|Dinari]] documents a US broker-dealer route.
- Issuer-sponsored shares can admit eligible US investors, usually behind KYC and a transfer-agent whitelist. Exodus token holders can only trade with holders who passed the [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]]'s AML/KYC and were whitelisted ([Exodus offering circular](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821534/000114036121012255/nt10013846x18_253g2.htm)). WisdomTree's WTGXX allows transfers only between verified, whitelisted [[concepts/glossary#wallet|wallets]] ([WisdomTree FAQ](https://dataspanapi.wisdomtree.com/pdr/documents/WEBSITE_FUND_DETAILS/WDT/US/EN-US/WTGXX_3/)).
- Tokenized Securities Venues under the [[concepts/innovation-exemption|Innovation Exemption]] are permissioned: access is limited to approved participants ([SEC order 34-106402](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf)). Securitize's 12 Nov 2026 comment letter argues that a pool allowlist only screens at the point of trade, so a verified buyer can withdraw to a self-hosted wallet and send the token to a sanctioned person; it asks the SEC to require permissioning in the token itself, with freeze, burn and reissue as the fallback ([Securitize](https://www.sec.gov/comments/S7-2026-32/4927-1134705-4042498.pdf)). That is advocacy, not a change to the order.

## What this means for holders
- Most offshore tokens ([[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]], [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]], Robinhood, Coinbase, bStocks) exclude US persons; check the issuer page for the exact country list.
- US routes run through registered firms: Dinari as [[concepts/glossary#broker-dealer|broker-dealer]], Superstate as [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]] for native shares, or exchange-listed tokenized shares via the [[concepts/glossary#dtc|DTC]] pilot.
- Where you can buy is a property of the issuer and the platform together: see [[topics/rules-by-jurisdiction|Rules by jurisdiction]].

*Reference information only, not investment advice.*

- <https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/exorders/2026/34-106402.pdf>

- <https://www.alsobrooks.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Alsobrooks_Warner_Cortez_Masto_Gallego_SEC_Innovation_Exemption_Tokenization_Letter_11-12-2026_@_02-10_PM.pdf>

# Coinbase B20
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/b20
description: B20 is the token format Coinbase uses for its tokenized stocks on Base.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-10-25

*In plain English: B20 is the token format Coinbase uses for its tokenized stocks on Base.*

B20 is the Base-native token standard that Coinbase's tokenized stocks use ([Base](https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks); [Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). It is designed to work for any asset; stocks are one use case.

## Design
- A superset of [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]], built as Rust precompiles and shipped in Base's Beryl upgrade ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)). Standard ERC-20 methods and events work.
- Two variants: **Asset** (6-18 decimals, with a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]]) and **[[concepts/glossary#stablecoin|Stablecoin]]** (6 decimals) ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).
- Built-in controls: transfer policies, freeze-and-reissue, roles, memos, supply caps and permit ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).
- Audited by Base and Spearbit, per the docs ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20)).

## Tokenized stocks on B20
- **Multiplier**: one token does not always equal one share. Cash dividends are converted to shares and the multiplier rises (e.g. 1.02) ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). Scheduled changes use ERC-8056 `updateUIMultiplier`; the instant `updateMultiplier` is deprecated and kept as a failsafe.
- **Identification**: integrators should identify tokens by contract address, not ticker, and watch the `B20Created` event. A public, keyless API returns addresses, supply, multipliers, ISINs and Chainlink reference values ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).
- **Access**: secondary transfers are permissionless; [[concepts/glossary#kyc|KYC]] applies to Authorized Participants who [[concepts/glossary#mint|mint]] and [[concepts/glossary#redeem|redeem]] ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)).

See [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks|Coinbase tokenized stocks]], [[topics/corporate-actions-and-dividends|corporate actions]] and [[standards/erc-3643|ERC-3643]] for a permissioned alternative.

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://blog.base.org/tokenized-stocks>
- <https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20>
- <https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks>

# ERC-1400 / ERC-1410
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/erc-1400
description: ERC-1400 is an older, draft set of Ethereum rules for security tokens that can block or force transfers.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-11-12

*In plain English: ERC-1400 is an older, draft set of Ethereum rules for security tokens that can block or force transfers.*

ERC-1400 (draft, 2018) is an umbrella suite: ERC-1594 (transfer validation, off-chain data), ERC-1643 (documents), ERC-1644 (controller/forced transfers) and ERC-1410 (partitions) ([spec](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md)). ERC-1410 defines balanceOfByPartition, transferByPartition and operator transfers, i.e. "partially fungible" balances useful for lockups and share classes ([ERC-1410](https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1410.md)).

ConsenSys UniversalToken is a reference implementation with certificate-based validation ([GitHub](https://github.com/ConsenSys/ERC1400)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1400.md>
- <https://github.com/SecurityTokenStandard/EIP-Spec/blob/master/eip/eip-1410.md>
- <https://github.com/ConsenSys/ERC1400>

# ERC-3643 (T-REX)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/erc-3643
description: ERC-3643 is an Ethereum token standard that only lets approved, identity-checked wallets hold or receive the token.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-11-18

*In plain English: ERC-3643 is an Ethereum token standard that only lets approved, identity-checked wallets hold or receive the token.*

ERC-3643 is a final EIP. It extends the basic [[concepts/glossary#erc-20|ERC-20]] token with permissions: transfers can be conditional, paused or frozen, forced, or recovered.

A transfer only goes through if two checks pass ([EIP-3643](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643)):
- the **Identity Registry** confirms both parties hold valid ONCHAINID claims, and
- the modular **Compliance** contract approves it.

Compliance modules cover limits such as country, holder count and balances ([ERC-3643 docs](https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/permissioned-tokens)). Reference implementation: [GitHub](https://github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643).

Cross-chain compliance (4 Nov 2026): Apex Group, Chainlink, T-REX Network and the ERC-3643 Association demonstrated a compliance framework for an onchain bond aligned with Swift standards, in which identity, investor eligibility and transfer rules are set once at the asset level and reused across blockchains; Chainlink's CCIP carries ERC-3643 tokens between chains. Swift joined the ERC-3643 Association as part of the initiative. This was a bond demonstration, not a stock ([ERC-3643 Association](https://www.erc3643.org/news/interoperable-compliance-for-on-chain-capital-markets-aligned-with-swift-standards)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643>
- <https://docs.erc3643.org/erc-3643/smart-contracts-library/permissioned-tokens>
- <https://github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643>
- <https://www.erc3643.org/news/interoperable-compliance-for-on-chain-capital-markets-aligned-with-swift-standards>

# Solana Token-2022 extensions
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/standards/solana-token-2022
description: Token-2022 is Solana's token program with optional add-ons that tokenized stocks use for compliance and splits.
type: standard
last_checked: 2026-11-12

*In plain English: Token-2022 is Solana's token program with optional add-ons that tokenized stocks use for compliance and splits.*

Token-2022 adds extensions including transfer hook, permanent delegate, default account state, scaled UI amount and metadata ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions)).
- **Transfer hook**: a custom program runs on every transfer; ExtraAccountMetaList resolves extra accounts. This is Solana's equivalent of identity-gated compliance checks ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook)).
- **Scaled UI amount**: a [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] changes the displayed balance without changing raw balances; used for splits and reinvested dividends ([Solana](https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/scaled-ui-amount)).
Ondo Stocks are available on Solana, and some wallets show a display [[concepts/glossary#multiplier|multiplier]] there ([Ondo overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)). The current Ondo API overview states that Ondo Stocks on Solana are issued as SPL Token-2022 tokens ([Ondo API overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/api-reference/overview), retrieved 12 Nov 2026); the current Ondo Stocks overview and technical docs do not name the token standard.

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions>
- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/transfer-hook>
- <https://solana.com/docs/tokens/extensions/scaled-ui-amount>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview>
- <https://docs.ondo.finance/api-reference/overview>

# BUIDL (adjacent fund precedent)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/buidl-precedent
description: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, is an early example that later stock-token projects copied.
type: comparison
last_checked: 2026-11-20

*In plain English: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, is an early example that later stock-token projects copied.*

BlackRock's BUIDL fund (launched 20 Mar 2024) used Securitize as [[concepts/glossary#transfer-agent|transfer agent]], tokenization platform and placement agent ([Nasdaq PR](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/blackrock-launches-its-first-tokenized-fund-buidl-on-the-ethereum-network-2024-03-20)). Adjacent to equities: a fund, not a stock. See also [[issuers/wisdomtree|WisdomTree]] (funds).

On 12 Nov 2026 Securitize and Ethena Labs announced a 24/7 liquidity facility for BUIDL, supported by Ethena and operated through Securitize. It lets eligible investors exchange BUIDL for supported stablecoins, including USDC, and convert those stablecoins back into BUIDL, outside traditional market hours. The facility launches with \$50 million of initial liquidity (\$25 million USDC and \$25 million BUIDL). The release says up to another \$50 million may be made available within about an hour, and that references to a "\$100 million facility" describe maximum capacity, not an amount continuously funded or immediately available ([Securitize](https://investors.securitize.io/news/news-details/2026/Securitize-and-Ethena-Launch-100-Million-Liquidity-Facility-for-BlackRocks-BUIDL/default.aspx)).

A later bank example is HSBC's 19 Nov 2026 launch of Class SD, a tokenised unit class of a Hong Kong dollar money market fund that eligible customers can buy with HSBC RedCoin from a minimum of HKD 100; see [[concepts/international|International regimes]] ([HSBC](https://www.about.hsbc.com.hk/news-and-media/hsbc-redcoin-expands-into-wealth-with-tokenised-fund-access)).

## Sources
Public originals for the facts on this page.

- <https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/blackrock-launches-its-first-tokenized-fund-buidl-on-the-ethereum-network-2024-03-20>
- <https://investors.securitize.io/news/news-details/2026/Securitize-and-Ethena-Launch-100-Million-Liquidity-Facility-for-BlackRocks-BUIDL/default.aspx>
- <https://www.about.hsbc.com.hk/news-and-media/hsbc-redcoin-expands-into-wealth-with-tokenised-fund-access>

# Implementations compared by model
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/implementations-by-model
description: A side-by-side table of tokenized stock projects, grouped by legal model, including what a holder can redeem the token into.
type: comparison
last_checked: 2026-11-21

*In plain English: A side-by-side table of tokenized stock projects, grouped by legal model, including what a holder can redeem the token into.*

Classification follows the [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|SEC staff taxonomy]]. Details and sources are on each linked page. Jersey Stock Tokens and EU Classic Stock Tokens are different products (both are on the Robinhood page). Cells for Coinbase, Backpack, bStocks, DTC and the venues use existing vault sources; this pass did not re-open those issuer redemption docs.

| Implementation | Model | Key mechanism | What can you redeem into? |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell\|Superstate Opening Bell]] | Issuer-sponsored | SEC-registered transfer agent; onchain cap table | The token is the share on the company's own register (SEC-registered transfer agent); a native share, not a wrapper ([Galaxy](https://www.galaxy.com/newsroom/galaxy-superstate-launch-glxy-tokenized-public-shares)). No separate cash-or-share redeem. |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize (issuer shares)]] | Issuer-sponsored | Transfer agent book entry | The investor, not Cede & Co., is the registered holder on the issuer's books ([Securitize letter](https://www.sec.gov/comments/SR-DTC-2026-012/srdtc2026012-1108719-3924407.pdf)). |
| [[infrastructure/fairmint\|CNTN via Fairmint]] | Issuer-sponsored | SEC-registered transfer agent keeps the official onchain register on Canton; trades on [[platforms-venues/tsv-llc\|TSV LLC]] | The token is recorded on the company's own register by its SEC-registered transfer agent ([CNTN release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/first-trades-of-tokenized-us-equity-under-sec-innovation-exemption-executed-on-the-canton-network-302929795.html)). |
| [[issuers/securitize\|Securitize Stocks]] | Custodial entitlement | UCC Art. 8 via broker-dealer; Solana PropAMM | UCC Article 8 entitlement; where available, holders can convert to direct registration ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-launches-global-onchain-trading-of-us-stocks-with-security-entitlements-302902107.html)). |
| [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase B20]] | Custodial claim | Beneficial claim; Alpaca custody | Redemption rights only for Vested Holders, per the prospectus (see the [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase]] page). |
| [[issuers/dinari\|Dinari dShares]] | Broker-dealer mirror record | Tokens mirror off-chain brokerage books | Sell/burn for payment tokens (stablecoin proceeds); the custodian sells the share. No in-kind delivery found in issuer docs ([placing orders](https://docs.dinari.com/docs/placing-orders); [dShares](https://dinari.com/dshares)). KYC required. US tokens are currently non-transferable ([US docs](https://docs.dinari.com/docs/us)). |
| [[issuers/backpack\|Backpack Securities]] | Custodial entitlement + token | Art. 8 entitlement at the broker; separate 1:1 Solana token | 1:1 into the underlying entitlement by depositing the token to a Backpack account ([Backpack](https://learn.backpack.exchange/articles/what-is-backpack-securities)). |
| [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot\|DTC Tokenized Entitlements]] | Custodial entitlement (post-trade) | DTC participants; NAL | Conversion orders via UI/API, Monday–Friday 2 a.m.–6 p.m. ET, targeting 15 minutes or less ([DTCC At-a-Glance](https://communications.dtcc.com/rs/669-QIL-921/images/DTCC%20Tokenization%20Service%20At-a-Glance.pdf)). |
| [[issuers/ondo-global-markets\|Ondo Stocks]] | Synthetic / note | BVI SPV notes; economic exposure | Direct platform redeem with Ondo for USDon or USDC; notes, not title to the share ([investing and redeeming](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/investing-and-redeeming); [legal](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)). $1 minimum; KYC. Ondo also says approved institutions can use an in-kind conversion through Alpaca's ITN that returns shares rather than cash ([Ondo](https://ondo.finance/blog/ondo-stocks-as-collateral-on-spout)). |
| [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood Stock Tokens]] | Synthetic / debt security | Jersey issuer; no rights in underlying | Jersey Stock Tokens: cash only; the prospectus excludes physical delivery of the underlying ([base prospectus, 25 June 2026](https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/rhj_base_prospectus.pdf)). Ordinary holders generally sell on the secondary market; direct issuer redemption only in limited no-AP or issuer-notice cases, plus KYC/AML. EU Classic Stock Tokens (separate product): cannot redeem for shares; sell back to Robinhood Europe in the app for EUR (0.10% FX fee, €1 minimum) ([KID, 1 July 2026](https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/stock_tokens_kid_eu.pdf); [EU FAQ](https://robinhood.com/eu/en/support/articles/stock-tokens-faq/)). |
| [[issuers/bstocks\|bStocks]] | Synthetic / certificate | ADGM certificates over shares | 1:1 conversion between supported stock holdings and bStocks (per Binance announcement, via Zerion) ([Binance](https://www.binance.com/my-MM/square/post/332985202800018)). |
| [[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]] | Backed tracker | Jersey issuer; multiplier | After KYC, redeem with the issuer for USDC, USDG or USDT ($5,000 minimum stated for direct issuer flow; fees currently 0) or in-kind shares into an Alpaca brokerage account via xPort ([FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions); [Market Flow](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/issuance-and-redemption/market-flow); [xPort](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/issuance-and-redemption/in-kind-flow-xport)). Tracker certificates, not shareholder rights. Most users exit on secondary markets. |
| [[platforms-venues/hyperliquid-equity-perps\|Equity perps (HIP-3, Ostium)]] | Synthetic derivative | Perpetual futures; cash margin, no share held | N/A — cash-settled perpetual; no share held ([Ostium](https://docs.ostium.com/protocol/how-ostium-works); [[platforms-venues/hyperliquid-equity-perps\|equity perps]]). |
| [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv\|OKXICE TSV]] | Venue (TSV) | Permissioned [[concepts/glossary#amm-automated-market-maker\|AMM]] under the Innovation Exemption; announced launch beginning 23 Nov 2026 ([OKX](https://www.okx.com/en-us/learn/okxice-tsv-launch)) | N/A (venue). |
| [[platforms-venues/formation-securities\|Formation Securities]] | Venue (TSV, notice filed; not yet trading) | Permissioned Orca AMM on Solana under the Innovation Exemption ([Formation notice](https://www.formationsecurities.com/notice.pdf)) | N/A (venue). |
| [[concepts/post-trade-reg-nms-model\|Nasdaq / NYSE]] | Venue (exchange) | Same book, DTC settlement | N/A (exchange; DTC settlement). |

## Why does the same stock have several tokens?

The same listed stock can have more than one token, issued by different firms, with different legal rights. Display tickers often use a suffix, but that is an issuer convention, not a single standard, and onchain metadata can change. Identify a token by its contract address, not by the ticker alone. See [[concepts/glossary#ticker-suffix|ticker suffix]] ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks); [Backpack listings](https://learn.backpack.exchange/blog/tokenized-nvidia-nvda)). Examples below use widely cited large-cap names already on this wiki. This is not a complete token list, and a suffix is not documented here unless an official page or official API retrieved on 12 Nov 2026 showed it.

| Pattern | Example | Issuer | Typical chains | What you hold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Suffix `x` | NVDAx, TSLAx | [[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]] (Backed) | Solana, Ethereum, TON, Ink | A tracker certificate: economic exposure, not shareholder rights ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq); [xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions)). The `x` ending is used throughout Kraken's FAQ; the official issuer FAQ does not itself define a suffix rule. |
| Suffix `on` | TSLAon | [[issuers/ondo-global-markets\|Ondo Stocks]] | Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana | A structured note, designed for economic exposure, "not direct title" to the underlying assets ([Ondo overview](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/overview)). Ondo documents the `on` suffix as official ("onchain or Ondo"). |
| Suffix `c` | TSLAc, NVDAc | [[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase]] | Base | A beneficial claim on a share held in bankruptcy-remote custody, not a share on the company's register ([Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). Every symbol in Coinbase's public tokenized-stocks API list retrieved on 12 Nov 2026 ended in `c` (338 tokens; [Base docs](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks)). |
| Often `rh` onchain; official API uses the bare ticker | NVDArh (onchain display); API example AAPL | [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood]] Stock Tokens | Robinhood Chain | Jersey Stock Tokens are debt securities and give no rights in the underlying shares, as already recorded on the issuer page. The official Stock Token API uses the underlying ticker with no suffix ([Stock Token APIs](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/stock-token-apis/)). Onchain display symbols such as NVDArh are attributed to Ondo's 27 Oct 2026 blog ([Ondo](https://ondo.finance/blog/ondo-stocks-live-on-robinhood-chain-and-uniswap)), not to that API page. |
| No suffix | $NVDA (token name "Nvidia - Backpack Securities") | [[issuers/backpack\|Backpack Securities]] | Solana | An Article 8 entitlement plus a 1:1 token, as already recorded on the issuer page. Listings use the cash-equity ticker and tell readers to check the token name and address ([Backpack](https://learn.backpack.exchange/blog/tokenized-nvidia-nvda)). |

Suffixes for other issuers on the table above (including Dinari, bStocks and Securitize) are not listed here because official docs retrieved for this update did not define one.

How the broker-backed and issuer-sponsored models differ in practice (where the share sits, who creates supply, lost keys): [[build/trading-reference-architecture#broker-backed-vs-issuer-sponsored-register|Broker-backed vs issuer-sponsored register]]. How each venue matches and settles: [[comparisons/trading-venue-architectures|Trading venue architectures]].

Kimber Digital Securities LLC, a Plume affiliate, said on 10 Nov 2026 that it is now an SEC-registered broker-dealer and a FINRA member. It plans tokens that would record a customer's security entitlement against the broker-dealer, with the firm holding a matching entitlement at DTC; it describes this as the same legal interest investors hold today and "not a wrapper," and says investors could use ACATS to move portfolios between offchain and onchain formats. The release states that access to DTC tokenized entitlements and related capabilities is under development and may not yet be available; it does not give a launch date ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/kimber-digital-securities-becomes-a-registered-broker-dealer-bringing-real-us-securities-onchain-302935166.html)).

## What are the four ways a stock token can be built?

In one reader-friendly lens, a stock token is wrapped, pooled, mirrored or natively issued.

The table above is grouped by the [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|SEC staff taxonomy]]. [Simon Taylor](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sytaylor_there-are-4-models-of-stock-tokens-each-share-7526006201432686592-ntwC) has described a reader-friendly lens with four models, each trading off shareholder rights, innovation and backward compatibility (LinkedIn post, retrieved 10 Nov 2026; short link: [lnkd.in/p/duAUZtYs](https://lnkd.in/p/duAUZtYs)). The mapping here is to rows this page already tracks. It is his framing, not a legal classification or this wiki's opinion.

**Wrapped.** His example is [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]]: a custodian holds the real share, the issuer (Backed) issues a token, and the holder does not get shareholder rights. Trade-off, in his words: this maximizes innovation and can work with any stock, at the cost of those rights. On this page, [[issuers/backpack|Backpack]]-style products sit nearby in that lens, though the table's legal grouping treats them as a custodial entitlement plus a separate token.

**Pooled.** His example is [[platforms-venues/okxice-tsv|OKXICE]]: a venue tokenizes real shares, and approved traders trade against a liquidity pool. Trade-off, in his telling: the design aims to be innovative, backward compatible and to preserve shareholder rights; under the Innovation Exemption, issuers can object to their stock being traded that way.

**Mirrored.** His example is [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTC Tokenized Entitlements]]: the original stock is immobilized, and the depository issues a token in its place. Trade-off, in his words: this maximizes backward compatibility and preserves shareholder rights, and trades off a lot of innovation.

**Natively issued.** His examples include [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]] (and Figure). On this table, [[infrastructure/fairmint|CNTN via Fairmint]] and [[issuers/securitize|Securitize issuer-sponsored shares]] are the other issuer-sponsored rows, where the token is the share on the company's own register. Trade-off, in his words: this maximizes innovation and rights, and gives up backward compatibility.

The wrapped and mirrored rows also differ in the claim a holder has. In a wrapped token such as [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]], a third-party issuer, Backed Assets (JE) Limited, issues a tracker certificate: the holder has that certificate, not the share itself, and it does not convey shareholder rights; the official issuer FAQ says the underlying stock is held by regulated custodians, without naming the firm ([xStocks FAQ](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/frequently-asked-questions); [xStocks multiplier docs](https://docs.xstocks.fi/developers/multipliers)). Kraken's FAQ, last updated 11 Nov 2026, names Alpaca Securities LLC as the custodian of the underlying shares and InCore Bank as a secondary custodian; Payward's 11 Nov 2026 release says GTN handles global execution and custody of the traditional assets that underpin each token. Those are separate company statements, recorded side by side on the [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] page ([Kraken FAQ](https://support.kraken.com/articles/xstocks-faq); [Payward](https://www.payward.com/press-release/xstocks-uk-eu-equities)). In [[infrastructure/dtcc-tokenization-pilot|DTC Tokenized Entitlements]], securities are held at DTC and official books and records remain with DTC; on a participant's instruction, DTC mints and delivers a token representing that participant's security entitlement to the held position ([DTCC At-a-Glance](https://communications.dtcc.com/rs/669-QIL-921/images/DTCC%20Tokenization%20Service%20At-a-Glance.pdf); [SEC no-action letter](https://www.sec.gov/files/tm/no-action/dtc-nal-121125.pdf)). Under the [[concepts/legal-taxonomy|SEC staff taxonomy]], that is a custodial security entitlement (for example, under UCC Article 8), so the token evidences an interest in the position at DTC rather than a separate instrument of a third-party issuer; the staff has also noted that holders of third-party-sponsored tokens may be exposed to risks with respect to that third party, such as bankruptcy, that a holder of the underlying security would not necessarily face ([SEC staff statement, 28 Jan 2026](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities)).

**Permissioned at the edges, open in the middle (announced design).** Exposure on Solana, announced 16 Nov 2026 by [[issuers/superstate-opening-bell|Superstate]], Formation and Corda, gates only minting and burning to authorized non-US persons; once minted, the tokens move permissionlessly in Solana DeFi. That differs from the issuer-sponsored rows above, where holders themselves must be approved. Its disclaimer says holders have no claim on the backing asset, the issuer or Superstate. No Exposure Token was live as of the announcement ([Superstate](https://superstate.com/newsroom/superstate-formation-and-corda-join-forces-to-launch-exposure-the-official-solana-rwa-launchpad); [Exposure](https://exposuretokens.com/)).

For a five-product view by legal claim, eligibility and redemption, see [[comparisons/tokenized-stocks-compared|Tokenized stocks compared]].


## How were Anthropic's tokenized products built? (IPO day, 19 Nov 2026)

Anthropic, PBC priced its IPO at \$83.00 per Class A share on 18 Nov 2026 (980,000,000 shares including selling stockholders) and listed on Nasdaq as "ANT" ([Form 424B4](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026074944/anthropicpbc-424b4.htm)). Several tokenized products tied to the stock were offered or planned for the same day. They use different legal models, and none of the sources retrieved describes any of them as issued or sponsored by Anthropic. Ondo says in its release that it is "not a participant in Anthropic's initial public offering" and that ANTon is not issued, sponsored or endorsed by Anthropic ([Ondo](https://www.prnewswire.co.uk/news-releases/ondo-stocks-to-launch-anton-with-247-mint-and-redeem-live-on-ipo-day-302943767.html)). The Coinbase prospectus says the Underlying Issuer "is not involved in the offer or sale of the Securities" ([prospectus](https://www.adgm.com/globalassets/market-disclosure/content/prospectus/coinbase-onchain-spv-ltd---prospectus-antc---18nov2026.pdf)). Bitget says rANT "is not issued, offered, or managed by Anthropic" and "has not been approved, sponsored, or endorsed by Anthropic" ([Bitget](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603899381)).

| Product | What you hold | Issuer / entity | Backing claim | Who can buy | Rights (vote, redemption) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ANTon** ([[issuers/ondo-global-markets\|Ondo Stocks]]) | A token giving exposure to Anthropic stock; Ondo says its tokens "are not themselves stocks" | Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited | Ondo says each token is "fully backed by the corresponding stock or ETF (together with cash in transit)" (platform-wide wording, not specific to ANTon) | "Eligible investors outside the U.S."; from \$1 | No right "to hold or receive" the underlying; no shareholder voting ([Ondo docs](https://docs.ondo.finance/ondo-stocks/legal-and-regulatory)); mint and redeem 24/7 on Ondo's platform ([Ondo release](https://www.prnewswire.co.uk/news-releases/ondo-stocks-to-launch-anton-with-247-mint-and-redeem-live-on-ipo-day-302943767.html)) |
| **ANTx** via Kraken "IPO Access" ([[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]]) | An xStocks tracker token; Kraken says "price exposure only" | Backed Assets (JE) Limited (xStocks); distributed by Kraken | Kraken: "backed 1:1 by the underlying share, held in custody by a regulated entity (Backed Assets (JE) Limited)" | Kraken clients in the EEA and most of the world; not the US or US persons, UK, Canada, Japan, Australia, New Zealand. Submit interest at the offering price plus a 5% spread; allocation "decided by the IPO underwriters", not guaranteed ([Kraken](https://support.kraken.com/articles/anthropic-ipo-access)) | "Do not carry voting rights"; no direct ownership. Redemption is not described in the IPO article |
| **Binance Wallet IPO campaign** (marketed as xStocks ANTx; delivered as ANTB) | Campaign terms as reported: price exposure only, without voting or dividend rights. Binance Wallet's 19 Nov update calls the tokens it delivered ANTB | Backed or its affiliates, as reported; Binance Wallet says it does not issue or hold the tokens | Reported: reserves may be cash or other eligible assets rather than the shares, and xStocks may deliver bStocks instead of ANTx ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/19/cz-says-tokenized-anthropic-is-coming-to-bnb-chain-on-ipo-day); [Bitcoin.com](https://news.bitcoin.com/exchanges/binance-wallet-500m-anthropic-ipo-xstocks-token-sale/)) | Binance Wallet users in a campaign, as reported: 100 USDC minimum, 500M USDC cap, 5% xStocks fee, allocation not guaranteed ([Bitcoin.com](https://news.bitcoin.com/exchanges/binance-wallet-500m-anthropic-ipo-xstocks-token-sale/)). Outcome, from Binance's own posts: all 500,002,764 USDC committed was returned, and an allocation of "roughly 2,957 Anthropic tokenized stocks (ANTB)" was distributed pro rata at no cost, plus a \$1,000,000 ANTB airdrop ([Binance](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/f37d1230c2e542fbb1872fcde3ebf140); [Binance Wallet](https://t.me/binance_wallet_announcements/1955)) | Reported: no voting or dividend rights. Binance's campaign FAQ page could not be captured, so the campaign terms stay labeled reported |
| **xANT** on OKX ([[issuers/xstocks-backed\|xStocks]]) | OKX "Unified Tokenized Stocks": "price exposure of an underlying stock", with a right to withdraw xStocks | OKX offers the asset; powered by xStocks, "Payward's tokenized equity framework"; "not a token issued by OKX" | None stated beyond the xStocks framework | Region-dependent; OKX says to "check the availability ... for your region in the app" ([OKX](https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-list-xant-for-spot-trading-and-convert-ant-pre-ipo-futures)) | "Does not represent ownership ... or confer shareholder rights such as voting"; withdrawal of xStocks on Solana or X Layer |
| **ANT dShares** ([[issuers/dinari\|Dinari]]) | Dinari's "tokenized representation of Anthropic stock"; in the US a secondary ledger, and issued tokens were "currently non-transferrable" in the docs last updated 22 Jun 2026 | Dinari (US broker-dealer structure; see issuer page) | Dinari: "backed by the underlying security" | "Eligible investors in the U.S. and more than 90 countries" through Dinari's app and partners. No direct IPO purchase: "Participation is through the secondary market once the stock begins trading" ([Dinari FAQ](https://docs.dinari.com/docs/anthropic-ipo-faqs); [US docs](https://docs.dinari.com/docs/us)) | Dinari's blog claims the model preserves "voting rights" and corporate actions, and Dinari and Broadridge announced proxy voting for eligible holders (issuer page). Its US docs describe a secondary ledger. Treat the ANT voting claim as Dinari's own: no ANT-specific legal document was found |
| **ANTc** ([[issuers/coinbase-tokenized-stocks\|Coinbase]] Onchain SPV) | "Anthropic CB Certificates (Certificates over Shares)", beneficial interests in the shares; "not direct investments in the Underlying" | Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd (ADGM); tokenisation entity Onchain Marketplace Ltd | Shares held by Alpaca Securities LLC as custodian | Offer only to Authorised Participants in the ADGM; others acquire in DeFi markets as Unvested Holders; not for US persons ([Coinbase prospectus](https://www.adgm.com/globalassets/market-disclosure/content/prospectus/coinbase-onchain-spv-ltd---prospectus-antc---18nov2026.pdf)) | "Only Vested Holders may exercise any rights" including redemption and voting; no direct voting right (issuer may "endeavour to vote" on Vested Holders' instructions); creation fee 0.01%, redemption fee 0.05% |
| **ANT** on Solana ([[issuers/backpack\|Backpack Securities]] via Sunrise, reported) | A 1:1 Solana token that Backpack says is a "distinct instrument" from the account's security entitlement | Backpack Securities as issuer, with Sunrise distributing, per Backpack's 11 Nov announcement as reported by [crypto.news](https://crypto.news/tokenized-anthropic-stock-solana-backpack-securities/); the X announcement itself was not retrieved | Backpack docs: every tokenized security "is redeemable 1:1 for the real underlying share" (generic wording, ANT not named) | Eligible verified Backpack users; not the US, UK, UAE, Japan or Backpack EU (issuer page) | Entitlement holders get "dividend eligibility, corporate action participation"; the sources do not say whether token holders vote. Redeem 1:1 by depositing the token ([Sunrise docs](https://docs.sunrise.xyz/equities/backpack-securities)) |
| **ANT** on Securitize Stocks ([[issuers/securitize\|Securitize]]) | A security entitlement: "not shares registered directly in the holder's name" | Securitize Markets, LLC, a registered broker-dealer (FINRA/SIPC); tokens issued on Solana | "Backed 1:1 by corresponding underlying securities held through Securitize Markets' brokerage infrastructure" | "Eligible investors in the United States, European Union (EU) and other permitted jurisdictions" ([Securitize](https://investors.securitize.io/news/news-details/2026/Securitize-Tokenizes-Anthropic-Stock-Onchain-on-First-Day-of-Public-Trading/default.aspx)) | "Economic benefits and voting entitlements passed through under the product terms"; holders "are not registered shareholders of Anthropic". USDC settlement, Jump Trading liquidity; trading "beyond traditional market hours", with 24/7 planned |
| **Anthropic Stock Token** ([[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood]], Robinhood Chain) | A tokenised debt security linked to Anthropic (Series 218, ISIN JE00C0C8R651); no legal or beneficial rights in the shares | Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited | Collateral "primarily comprises the Underlying", with Alpaca Securities LLC as custodian and broker; the shares "may be lent out" against collateral ([Final Terms](https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/rhj_final_terms_for_tokenised_debt_securities_linked_to_anthropic_pbc.pdf)) | Not the US or US persons; restricted in other places including Canada, the UK and Switzerland ([RHJ](https://docs.robinhood.com/rhj/product); [Vlad Tenev on X](https://x.com/vladtenev/status/2123560390759997721)). Only the Authorised Participant (Bitstamp Global Ltd.) subscribes from the issuer | "Not entitled to exercise voting rights"; dividends reach holders as the terms provide (multiplier). Investor fee 0.00% at issue; redemption amount based on the Nasdaq price |
| **ANTB** ([[issuers/bstocks\|bStocks]], listed on Binance) | An ADGM certificate; Binance says bStocks "are not stocks or shares" | bStocks issuer (BTECH Holdings, see issuer page); the ANT-specific prospectus was not found | Binance Wallet describes ANTB as "intended to be fully backed by real Anthropic shares held by a regulated custodian" ([Binance](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/f37d1230c2e542fbb1872fcde3ebf140)) | Binance users in permitted regions; not US persons; no public offer outside the ADGM ([Binance](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/830c320848af4257812d5b6e99e031f9)) | Spot ANTB/USDT from 18:00 UTC on 19 Nov (BNB Smart Chain). Direct stock holdings convert 1:1 with no fee, and for a limited time "eligible third-party tokenized securities" convert 1:1 into ANTB under a daily cap; accepted as margin collateral ([Binance](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c4a6afb79b32434a88e826b9632242c0)) |
| **rANT** ([[issuers/reality\|Reality]], listed on [[platforms-venues/bitget\|Bitget]] IPO Prime) | A tokenized stock; Bitget says holding rANT "is not equivalent to directly holding Anthropic shares" and does not automatically confer shareholder status or voting rights | Reality, per Bitget; offered through Bitget IPO Prime | Bitget's IPO Prime page: each token "maps 1:1 to a share" and Reality "custodies the underlying Anthropic shares"; Bitget's rANT page: "backed 1:1 by real shares held in custody with a licensed broker", and names Alpaca as Reality's broker partner | Eligible users in permitted regions; not offered to residents of restricted jurisdictions ([Bitget](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603899381)). US eligibility is not stated in the retrieved articles | No automatic shareholder status or voting rights; redemption "subject to the product documents," which were not retrieved ([Bitget](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603899381); [Bitget IPO Prime](https://www.bitget.com/spotlight/ipo-prime); [Bitget rANT page](https://www.bitget.com/price/anthropic-tokenized-stock-reality)) |
| **Pre-IPO perpetuals** (trade.xyz "ANT" on Hyperliquid; Kraken PF_ANTXUSD; OKX) | A cash-settled derivative contract. No share behind it | The trading venue | None. trade.xyz: "Pre-IPO Perpetuals are not shares ... not tokenized equity, securities entitlements, or rights to receive any security" | Varies by venue; Kraken's contracts offer up to 5x leverage | No ownership, voting, dividends or allocation rights. After listing, trade.xyz says the contract converts to a standard equity perpetual, "typically the first regular session after listing"; OKX converts its contracts in a 14:30-19:00 UTC window on 19 Nov; Kraken converts PF_ANTXUSD once there is a "viable index" ([trade.xyz](https://docs.trade.xyz/perpetuals/markets/pre-ipo-perpetuals.md); [Kraken](https://support.kraken.com/articles/pre-ipo-perpetual-futures-faq)) |

**What Anthropic says.** The 424B4 does not mention tokenized shares: a word search of the full text found no occurrence of tokenized shares, blockchain, onchain or stablecoin ([Anthropic 424B4](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026074944/anthropicpbc-424b4.htm)). Anthropic's Claude Help Center page on unauthorized stock sales, first published 11 Feb 2026 and written about private-stock transfers, says any third party selling Anthropic shares to the general public through "direct sales, 'forward contracts,' tokenized securities, or other mechanisms" is "likely offering an investment that may have no value due to our transfer restrictions" ([Claude Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13704655-unauthorized-anthropic-stock-sales-and-investment-scams)). The page does not say how that applies after the IPO. A second page on the IPO's retail offerings in Australia, Canada, parts of the EEA, Japan, Switzerland and the UK says Anthropic "has not authorized any other firm or platform to offer, or to advertise access to, shares in the proposed retail offerings" and lists the authorized brokers; no crypto exchange or tokenizer is on that list ([Claude Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17889756-anthropic-ipo-international-retail-brokers-and-selling-agents)). That page concerns shares in those offerings, not tokenized products, and does not mention them.

**Marketing names.** "IPO Access" (Kraken), the "IPO xStocks Campaign" (Binance Wallet) and "IPO Prime" (Bitget) are the venues' own names for their products. Kraken describes unallocated funds being refunded and allocation "decided by the IPO underwriters"; no source retrieved says what share allocation, if any, those venues or Backed received. The table records what each issuer or venue says; the tokens' legal claims are separate from the shares sold in the IPO.

## What happened on Anthropic's first trading day? (19 Nov 2026)

**On Nasdaq.** ANT opened at \$111.50 ([Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/newsroom/anthropic-marks-ipo-at-nasdaq)). Nasdaq's data shows a high of \$115.10, a low of \$92.72, a close of \$97.17 (17.07% above the \$83.00 IPO price) and volume of 857,312,300 shares ([Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/ant/historical)); other outlets printed slightly different volume totals. Nasdaq does not give the time of the first trade. Yahoo Finance reported that it came "nearly noon", with 108 million shares in the opening print ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-stocks-first-trade-was-worth-12-billion--34-above-its-ipo-price-171721561.html)), and SolanaFloor put it at 11:48 AM ET ([SolanaFloor](https://solanafloor.com/news/anthropics-81-3-b-ipo-breaks-space-x-s-record-as-early-ant-trading-volume-on-solana-tops-29-m)). Both timings are reported.

**IPO allocations through crypto venues.** Bitget said it received a final allocation of 153,774 Anthropic shares (VIP 137,494 at 11.26%; public 16,280 at 1.36%), per Bitget, with unallocated funds to be refunded by the stated UTC deadlines ([Bitget](https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603901105)). xStocks said it "received an allocation" but could "only partially fulfill xStocks IPO Access requests", that funds reserved for unfilled requests would be "released in full" and that no fees were charged ([xStocks on X](https://x.com/xStocksFi/status/2123440937213059208)). Kraken's support article, updated 19 Nov, tells participants to check their email for allocation information and gives no fill rate ([Kraken](https://support.kraken.com/articles/anthropic-ipo-access)). Binance Wallet said the allocation for its campaign was "not ideal relative to total user commitments". It returned all 500,002,764 USDC committed, in two batches, and distributed "roughly 2,957 Anthropic tokenized stocks (ANTB)" pro rata at no cost, plus a \$1,000,000 ANTB airdrop ([Binance](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/f37d1230c2e542fbb1872fcde3ebf140); [Binance Wallet](https://t.me/binance_wallet_announcements/1955)). The campaign was marketed as xStocks ANTx; the posts do not explain how the delivered tokens became ANTB.

**Token launches and prices.** Backpack's ANT went live on Solana through Sunrise at 11:55 AM ET, according to SolanaFloor (reported, [SolanaFloor](https://solanafloor.com/news/anthropics-81-3-b-ipo-breaks-space-x-s-record-as-early-ant-trading-volume-on-solana-tops-29-m)). Securitize announced ANT on Securitize Stocks the same day ([Securitize](https://investors.securitize.io/news/news-details/2026/Securitize-Tokenizes-Anthropic-Stock-Onchain-on-First-Day-of-Public-Trading/default.aspx)), and Robinhood's CEO said its Stock Token was live on Robinhood Chain ([Vlad Tenev on X](https://x.com/vladtenev/status/2123560388318912562)). Solana Compass reported Backpack's ANT at about \$95.50 at 2:22 PM ET against \$95.79 on Nasdaq at 2:00 PM ET ([Solana Compass](https://solanacompass.com/news/tokenized-anthropic-ant-goes-live-on-solana-on-ipo-day-from-backpack-ondo-xstocks-and-securitize)). The two prices are from different times, so they do not measure a premium or discount. No source retrieved gives token prices at the Nasdaq close, so this page states no premium or discount for any token.

**Supply on day 2, before the open (20 Nov, 9:05 AM ET).** Onchain reads show 74,945.7 Backpack ANT on Solana; 540.8 ANTon on Solana and 7,321.9 on Ethereum (229 Ethereum holders, per the Blockscout explorer); 78,355.5 ANTB on BNB Smart Chain; and 15,000,100 ANTx on Solana, the same as before the open on 19 Nov. Supply counts every token in existence, including any an issuer holds, so it is not a measure of investor holdings. Robinhood Chain and the other chains were not read.

**Volume and holders (reported).** SolanaFloor counted more than \$29M of tokenized ANT volume on Solana in about the first 90 minutes: Backpack's ANT \$26.8M, ANTx \$2.22M and ANTon \$39.1K ([SolanaFloor](https://solanafloor.com/news/anthropics-81-3-b-ipo-breaks-space-x-s-record-as-early-ant-trading-volume-on-solana-tops-29-m)). Solana Compass counted more than 8,000 holder accounts for Backpack's ANT and more than 350 for ANTx at 2:22 PM ET ([Solana Compass](https://solanacompass.com/news/tokenized-anthropic-ant-goes-live-on-solana-on-ipo-day-from-backpack-ondo-xstocks-and-securitize)). Uniswap's founder said Uniswap had traded "~83% of all tokenized ANT onchain", after more than \$10M in its first hours ([Hayden Adams on X](https://x.com/haydenzadams/status/2123533850366091566)). Solana's account posted "\$80M+" of ANT volume on Solana by 10:21 PM ET ([Solana on X](https://x.com/solana/status/2123617606754336987)), and Sunrise said ANT passed \$100M on Solana in under 24 hours ([Sunrise on X](https://x.com/sunrise/status/2123769864250695898)). Analyst Tom Wan counted about \$29M of tokenized ANT held onchain on day 2: xStocks \$9.2M, Backpack \$6.0M, bStocks \$5.7M, PreStocks \$5.0M, Robinhood \$2.7M, Ondo \$0.7M ([Tom Wan on X](https://x.com/tomwanhh/status/2123722051823563073)). These figures come from the parties themselves or third parties, use different scopes and cut-off times, and do not reconcile with each other.

**Volume and holdings by issuer (reported, added 21 Nov).** TechFlow, compiling GeckoTerminal, CoinGecko and exchange data for the 24 hours to 12:40 AM ET on 20 Nov, counted about \$106M of onchain DEX spot volume: Solana \$57.4M, Robinhood Chain \$36.3M, Base \$6.12M, BNB Chain \$5.9M and Ethereum \$0.45M. Including exchange spot, it ranked issuers Backpack ANT \$56.2M, Robinhood ANT \$36.3M, xStocks ANTx \$17M (Kraken about \$13.13M), bStocks ANTB \$15.6M (Binance spot about \$9.97M), Coinbase ANTc \$6.12M and Ondo ANTon \$0.92M, against about \$1.75B of ANT perpetual volume on Hyperliquid ([TechFlow](https://www.techflowpost.com/en-US/newsletter/145938)). The Entropy Advisors chart behind Tom Wan's holdings count lists token numbers per issuer and notes that the xStocks figure excludes \$39.1M held in Kraken's hot wallet ([Tom Wan on X](https://x.com/tomwanhh/status/2123722051823563073)). Its PreStocks figure (76,797 tokens, \$5.0M) implies about \$65 a token rather than \$97.17; PreStocks' pre-IPO token gives economic exposure only and, per its issuer, "trades at a discount to the public stock price" while the underlying shares are locked up ([PreStocks](https://prestocks.com/anthropic)).

**Days 1-2 by chain and by venue (reported, added 21 Nov evening).** Sunrise, which distributes Backpack's ANT, put two-day onchain spot DEX volume (19-20 Nov) at \$140M+ on Solana, \$64M on Robinhood Chain, \$27M on BNB Chain, \$17M on Base and about \$1M on Ethereum, citing Blockworks and GeckoTerminal ([Sunrise on X](https://x.com/sunrise/status/2124251486506885378)). It also said 36% of the \$170M+ of pool volume in Backpack's ANT through Sunrise, from the debut to 9 AM ET on 21 Nov, traded outside Nasdaq hours ([Sunrise on X](https://x.com/sunrise/status/2124302840164180038)). Raydium, citing Dune, counted 20.5K unique wallets trading tokenized Anthropic through its pools in the first 24 hours, ahead of Meteora (15.8K) and PumpSwap (11.6K); the counts overlap across AMMs ([Raydium on X](https://x.com/Raydium/status/2124161764132900988)). An Entropy Advisors chart posted by Tom Wan shows ANT at \$35.46M of Robinhood Chain DEX volume on 20 Nov, second to NVDA at \$37.71M ([Tom Wan on X](https://x.com/tomwanhh/status/2124105083101311239)). These are the parties' own or third-party figures with no published method; their windows differ from TechFlow's and they do not reconcile.

**Token prices at the close.** In the last minute before the 4:00 PM ET close, the largest pools on GeckoTerminal traded at \$96.53 (Backpack ANT), \$96.55 (ANTB) and \$96.67 (ANTc) against Nasdaq's \$97.17 on 19 Nov, and at \$88.03, \$88.14 and \$88.56 against \$88.91 on 20 Nov: 0.4% to 1.0% below the stock in each case ([GeckoTerminal](https://www.geckoterminal.com/solana/pools/4v6geaGFiFfQP9HbrxSLdwFKsda8V7jr99ADYq9NtJV1)). These are single-pool trade prices, not prices for size. Day 2 on Nasdaq: open \$89.86, high \$92.56, low \$83.05, close \$88.91, volume 400,460,300 shares ([Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/ant/historical)).

**Supply after day 2 (21 Nov, 1:06 AM ET).** Onchain reads show 67,364.95 Backpack ANT on Solana (down from 74,945.7 on 20 Nov), 84,024.3 ANTB on BNB Smart Chain (up from 78,355.5), 32,294.7 Robinhood Anthropic Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain (first read; Securities Ledger contract from the Final Terms), 14,935.96 ANTc on Base (address from block explorers, not from Coinbase's prospectus), 7,571.1 ANTon on Ethereum (270 holders, per Blockscout) and 525.5 on Solana, and ANTx on Solana unchanged at 15,000,100. Supply includes any tokens an issuer holds and is not a measure of investor holdings.

**Supply over the weekend (21 Nov, 11:14 PM ET).** With Nasdaq closed since Friday's close, onchain reads show 67,479.4 Backpack ANT on Solana (up from 67,364.95), 84,225.0 ANTB on BNB Smart Chain (up from 84,024.3) and 7,587.1 ANTon on Ethereum (300 holders, per Blockscout) and 540.6 on Solana. Robinhood's token (32,294.7), ANTc (14,935.96) and ANTx on Solana (15,000,100) were unchanged. Supply is not a measure of investor holdings.

**Perpetuals.** trade.xyz posted at 11:54 AM ET that its ANT market "has transitioned from an IPOP market and is now live with external pricing" ([trade.xyz on X](https://x.com/tradexyz/status/2123459924374024590)). Blockmetric, a data site, recorded \$6.3M of long and \$2M of short liquidations on that contract for the 19 Nov UTC day (reported; [Blockmetric](https://blockmetric.io/coins/xyz%3AANT/historical-data)). The sources retrieved do not confirm when OKX's or Kraken's contracts converted. OKX's own weekly recap on 21 Nov (1:30 AM ET) lists "Anthropic Tokenized stocks, global perps & X-Perps" as listed, without a date or region list ([OKX on X](https://x.com/okx/status/2124027544991080853)).

*Reference information only, not legal or investment advice.*

# Tokenized stock trading volume by venue (reported figures)
URL: https://edstokenizedsecuritiesrails.com/comparisons/reported-trading-volume-by-venue
description: Published trading-volume figures for tokenized stocks, by venue and issuer, each dated and sourced. Not like-for-like and not a league table.
type: comparison
last_checked: 2026-11-18

*In plain English: some venues publish trading volume, but the numbers are not like-for-like and this is not a league table.*

The figures below come from different dates, different product types and different methods. A cumulative total since launch is not a monthly total. DEX-only onchain volume is not the same as a company total that also counts centralized-exchange trading and mint or redemption. Value held (AUM, TVL, or market size) is not volume: the same tokens can change hands many times. Company-reported totals are the issuer's or venue's own claims; third-party analysis (for example Bitwise citing Allium) is not a primary disclosure by the venue; the IMF chapter is an official report but gives market size and trading patterns, not a venue volume table. Synthetic equity perpetuals are listed in a separate section because they are cash-settled contracts, often leveraged, with no share behind the trade.

How venues are built, rather than how much they have reported trading, is in [[comparisons/trading-venue-architectures|Trading venue architectures]].

## What tokenized-stock trading volumes have been published, and by which venues?

Published figures are not like-for-like and are not a league table. The largest dated spot or tokenized-stock prints found are these. [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens|Robinhood]] Chain Stock Tokens had \$14.05 billion of issuer-matched DEX volume from 1 Jul to 30 Sep 2026, according to Bitwise's Q4 2026 staking report (Allium data), including \$526 million in July, \$2.21 billion in August and \$11.31 billion in September. Payward said [[issuers/xstocks-backed|xStocks]] cumulative transaction volume across centralized and decentralized venues plus mint and redemption had passed \$45 billion as of 28 Oct 2026 (restated 11 Nov). [[issuers/ondo-global-markets|Ondo]] said Ondo Stocks had processed \$27 billion of cumulative volume across those same kinds of activity as of 14 Aug 2026. [[issuers/backpack|Backpack]] published \$5.3 billion-plus of onchain volume from 12 Jun to 18 Oct 2026, citing Blockworks and Birdeye. Many venues on this wiki have not published a volume series. Synthetic equity perps are listed separately.

| Venue or issuer | Metric | Figure | Period | Source | Source type | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[issuers/robinhood-stock-tokens\|Robinhood Chain / Stock Tokens]] | Issuer-matched DEX volume | \$526M (Jul); \$2.21B (Aug); \$11.31B (Sep); \$14.05B Q3 total | 1 Jul–30 Sep 2026 | [Bitwise Q4 2026 Staking Report](https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/static.bitwiseinvestments.com/Research/Bitwise-Staking-Report-Q4-2026.pdf) pp. 48, 52, citing Allium ([Bitwise Q4 2026 Staking Report](https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/static.bitwiseinvestments.com/Research/Bitwise-Staking-Report-Q4-2026.pdf)); summary page ([Bitwise](https://bitwiseinvestments.com/crypto-market-insights/the-bitwise-staking-report-q4-2026)). [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/tokenized-stocks-us-companies-object.html) (21 Oct) cited the same monthly totals. | Third-party analysis (Allium onchain data in a Bitwise report). Verified in the full report. Not a Robinhood primary disclosure. | DEX turnover on Robinhood Chain, not brokerage volume and not value held. Bitwise also gives average daily volume of \$17.0M / \$71.4M / \$377.1M (just over 22x from July to September) and says the priced circulating value was only \$27.9M / \$79.9M / \$160.8M, so the same tokens changed hands often. Pons pools that use Stock Tokens as a reserve are part of the DEX story.
